SUBTASK 32-41-00-870-001
(3) Release the brake pedals or the parking brake if it is set.
SUBTASK 32-41-00-870-002
(4) Make sure that all of the normal (System B) hydraulic fuses are not set.
(a) Operate the brake pedals several times.
(b) Look for movement of the brake wear indicator pins to make sure that all of the brakes
operate.
SUBTASK 32-41-00-860-005
(5) Remove the external hydraulic pressure for the normal (System B) hydraulic system, do this
task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805.
SUBTASK 32-41-00-870-003
(6) Make sure that the fluid in the normal (System B) hydraulic reservoir is at the correct level, do
this task: Hydraulic Reservoir Servicing, TASK 12-12-00-610-801.
(a) If the normal (System B) hydraulic reservoir needs to be filled, do this task: Hydraulic

32-41-00-870-804Normal (System B) Hydraulic System Brake Fuse TestPDF p. 1379
5. Normal (System B) Hydraulic System Brake Fuse Test
(Figure 201, Figure 202)
A. General
(1) This task provides instructions to test each hydraulic brake fuse for the normal hydraulic brake
system. There is one fuse for each brake for the normal hydraulic system. Each fuse must
pass a specific quantity of hydraulic fluid before it closes. For this task, each brake for the main
landing gear must be bled to check the fuse for that brake.

32-41-00-870-805Alternate (System A) Hydraulic System Brake Fuse TestPDF p. 1381
6. Alternate (System A) Hydraulic System Brake Fuse Test
(Figure 201, Figure 202)
A. General
(1) This task provides instructions to test each hydraulic brake fuse for the alternate hydraulic
brake system. There is one fuse for the two brakes on each main landing gear for the alternate
hydraulic system. Each fuse must pass a specific quantity of hydraulic fluid before it closes.
For this task, only one brake for the each main landing gear must be bled to check the fuse for
that brake.

32-41-00-820-801Hydraulic Brake System - AdjustmentPDF p. 1385
2. Hydraulic Brake System - Adjustment
(Figure 501)
A. General
(1) The landing gear brake system can be adjusted with the airplane on or off jacks.
(2) The hydraulic pressure can be 'On' or 'Off' during adjustment.
(3) The landing gear brake system must be adjusted with the brakes off.
(4) If rig pin tools are not available, use pins that are 0.309 in. (7.85 mm) - 0.311 in. (7.90 mm) in
diameter.

(1) Adjust the brake pedal bus [1], do these steps:
(a) Disconnect the right ends of the pushrods [2] from the brake pedal bus [1].
1) Remove the nuts [13], washers [12], bolts [8], and bushings [9] to disconnect the
pushrods [2] from the crank arm clevis [11].
NOTE: The forward pushrod has a centerline slip fit joint that is used for
installation/removal only.
2) If it is necessary, remove the screws [28], washers [29], and nuts [30] to adjust the
length of the forward pushrod [2].
(b) Install the rig pin LGB1, F70207-14, from rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, through the left beam
structure and brake control bellcranks [4].
NOTE: It is necessary for the rig pin to remain installed for the cable adjustment.
(c) Install the rig pin LGB2, F70207-14, from rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, through the right
beam structure and brake control bellcranks [4].
NOTE: It is necessary for the rig pin to remain installed for the cable adjustment.
(d) Loosen the jam nuts [7] on the ends of the pushrods [2].
(e) Adjust the length of the pushrods [2] by turning the rod ends [10], until the bolts [8] for the
pushrods [2] can be installed freely through the crank arm clevis [11].
1) Make sure that the threads of the rod ends [10] can be seen for at least half of the
inspection holes, or there are no more than 15 exposed threads between the jam
nut [7] and the bearing.
NOTE: This will make sure that the threads of the rod ends correctly engage the
pushrods.
(f) Install the bushings [9], bolts [8], washers [12], and nuts [13] to connect the pushrods [2]
to the crank arm clevis [11].
(g) Make sure that the rig pins LGB1 and LGB2 move freely through the rig pin holes.
(h) Tighten the jam nuts [7] on the rod ends [10].
WARNING
MAKE SURE TO ENGAGE THE FORWARD PUSHROD AFTER THE
ADJUSTMENT. IF YOU DO NOT ENGAGE THE PUSHROD, IT CAN
CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
1) If it is necessary, install the screws [28], washers [29], and nuts [30] when
adjustment of the pushrod [2] is complete.
(i) If the brake cables will not be adjusted, remove rig pins LGB1 and LGB2 from the brake
control bellcrank [4].

1) Remove the turnbuckle locking clips [5] from the turnbuckles [6].
2) Turn the turnbuckles [6] to reduce the tension.
3) Alternate the adjustment between the cables to make sure that the tension in each
cable does not differ by more than 50 lbf (222 N) at any time.
(b) Adjust the aft pushrod [2] on the brake pedal bus [1].
1) Loosen the jam nut [7] on the right end of the pushrod [2].
2) Remove the nut [13], washer [12], bolt [8], and bushing [9] to disconnect the aft
pushrod [2] from the crank arm clevis [11].
(c) Adjust the forward pushrod [2] on the brake pedal bus [1].
1) Create a cross hair, consisting of two lines, with a fine tip felt pen at the junction of
the two rods:
NOTE: This will be a reference point for future adjustments.
a) Make the cross-hair before the screws [28] are removed.
b) Put one line horizontally across both tubes, halfway between the screw head
and nut.
c) Put the other line around the tube where the smaller tube meets the larger
tube to complete the cross hair.
d) Make sure that the pushrod end inspection hole is not open.
2) Loosen the jam nut [7] on the right end of the forward pushrod [2].
3) Remove the screws [28], washers [29], and nuts [30] in the center of the
pushrod [2].
a) Keep the screws [28], washers [29], and nuts [30] for the reassembly after the
pushrod [2] adjustment.
(d) Install rig pin LGB1, F70207-14, from rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, through the left beam
structure and brake control bellcrank [4].
NOTE: It is necessary for the rig pin to remain installed for the cable adjustment.
(e) Install rig pin LGB2, F70207-14, from rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, through the right beam
structure and brake control bellcrank [4].
NOTE: It is necessary for the rig pin to remain installed for the cable adjustment.
(f) Push the aft pushrod [2] to the left to take up the tolerance.
(g) Push the right side crank arm clevis [11] to the left to take up the tolerance.
(h) Align the right rod end [10] fastener with the right side crank arm clevis [11]:
1) Turn the rod end [10].
2) Install the fastener.
a) Do not install the washer or nut at this time.
(i) Turn the pushrod [2] to lengthen or shorten the forward pushrod [2] to get the original
cross hair position.
1) Install only one screw [28], washer [29], and nut [30] at this time.

 ALL

(j) With the left rig pin installed, slowly remove the right rig pin and observe the forward and

1) If the pushrods [2] move, do these steps:

b) Install the right rig pin again.
c) Repeat the right rig pin removal.
<1> If the pushrod [2] movement is more than before, do these steps:
<a> Shorten the aft pushrod [2] to the previous length, then one turn
shorter.
<b> Repeat the rig pin installation and removal.
<2> Select the position that has the least pushrods [2] movement.
(k) Do a check of the rig pin fit.
NOTE: The rig pins will be biased in the hole. This means the rig pins will support the
weight of the pedals and bus structure and not be entirely free.
1) Make sure that the rig pin does not bind or needs excessive force to install or

(l) Install the remaining fasteners to complete the installation of the forward pushrod [2] and

1) For the aft pushrod [2], install the bolt [8], bushing [9], washer [12], and nut [13] to

2) Tighten the both jam nuts [7] for the aft pushrod [2].
3) For the forward pushrod [2], install the remaining screw [28], washer [29], and
nut [30].
a) Tighten the nuts [30] to snug plus 1/4 turn.
4) For the forward pushrod [2], tighten the jam nuts [7].
5) Make sure that the threads of the rod ends [10] can be seen for at least half of the

nut [7] and bearing.
NOTE: This will make sure that the threads of the rod ends correctly engage the
pushrods.
6) If no further adjustments are necessary, increase the tension in the cables per the

adjustment between the cables to make sure that the tension in each cable
does not differ by more than 50 lbf (222 N) at any time.
NOTE: This will keep the rig pins from bending.

(h) Tighten the jam nuts [19] on the two ends of the control rod [20].
(i) If the brake cables will not be adjusted, remove rig pin LGB3 or LGB4 from the rig pin
holes for the applicable brake metering valves.

(4) Adjust the left brake metering valve [21] and right brake metering valve [27], do these steps:

2) Remove the retainer [23].
3) Remove the bushing [24] from the crank [25].

1) Use the rigging pin kit, SPL-9118, to install the rig pin LGB3, rigging pin kit,

2) Use the rigging pin kit, SPL-9118, to install the rig pin LGB4, rigging pin kit,

3) Adjust the control rod [20] to obtain a rig pin slip fit.
4) Install the bushing [24] in the crank [25].
a) Install the retainer [23] to hold the bushing [24].
5) Install the bolt [22], washer [26], and nut [18] to connect the control rod [20] to the
crank [25] for the applicable brake metering valve.
6) Make sure that the rig pin LGB3 or rig pin LGB4 moves freely through the rig pin
holes.
(c) If the rigging pin kit, SPL-9118, is not available, to install the rig pin, do these steps:
NOTE: The rig pin will move from the neutral position when the crank position changes if
the brake cables are adjusted without the rigging pin kit, SPL-9118.
1) Install the bushing [24] in the crank [25].
a) Install the retainer [23] to hold the bushing [24].
2) Install the bolt [22], washer [26], and nut [18] to connect the control rod [20] to the
crank [25] for the applicable brake metering valve.
3) Insert the rig pin.
4) Adjust the control rod [20] by turning the threaded control rod [20] only, all the way
in one direction until the rig pin contacts the crank [25].
5) Reverse the adjustment direction and count the turns until the rig pin contacts the
other side of the crank [25].
6) Divide the number of turns by 2 and reverse the rod adjustment direction again.
NOTE: This will position the rig pin in the neutral position in the crank.
(d) Tighten the jam nut [19] on the two ends of the control rod [20].
(e) If the brake cables will not be adjusted, remove rig pin LGB3 or LGB4 from the rig pin
holes for the left brake metering valve [21] and right brake metering valve [27].
 ALL

(5) Adjust the brake cables for the left side and the right side, do these steps:
NOTE: It is recommended that airplanes supplied with the cables that contain higher zinc
coating (Grade D or Grade K) be re-tensioned 3 to 4 months into service. This will
bring the tension of the control cables within the desired range. After the cables are
re-tensioned, the high zinc cables will continue to relax at a rate that is equivalent to
other conformed cables.
(a) Make sure that the rig pins LGB1 and LGB2 are installed in the bellcrank rig pin holes [3]

 ALL

tensiometer, COM-1553, or high tension cable tensiometer, COM-1554, to the value
shown in Table 501.
1) Alternate the adjustment between the LGB1A cable and LGB1B cable for the left
side and the LGB2A cable and LGB2B cable for the right side.

32-41-00-710-801Normal and Alternate Brake Application - Functional TestPDF p. 1401
3. Normal and Alternate Brake Application - Functional Test
A. General
(1) This procedure does an operation test of these systems:
(a) The operation of the brakes with hydraulic power supplied by the NORMAL (System B)
brake hydraulic system.
(b) The operation of the brakes with hydraulic power supplied by the ALTERNATE (System
A) brake hydraulic system.
(2) The brake pedal force and angle will also be checked in this task.

CAN RETRACT. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS, AND DAMAGE

WARNING

(a) To test the normal (System B) brake system, only pressurize the system B hydraulic
system.
(b) To test the alternate (System A) brake system, only pressurize the system A hydraulic
system.
NOTE: The normal hydraulic system (System B) must not be pressurized for this test.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
F. Procedure
NOTE: The steps that follow are applicable for the normal and alternate brake systems. The system
that is tested depends on which hydraulic system is pressurized.
SUBTASK 32-41-00-710-008
(1) Measure the brake pedal force and travel for each brake pedal.
(a) Make sure that each pedal meets the requirements in Table 1.
(b) Attach a digital protractor, STD-1232, to the brake pedal to measure the travel (position).
1) Make sure that the digital protractor, STD-1232, is set to zero.
(c) Attach a spring scale or brake pedal measuring equipment, SPL-2555, to measure pedal
forces.
1) Make sure that the force gage is set to zero.

*[1] *[2]

(Deg)
Brake Pedal Force Brake Pedal Force Brake Pressure

(d) Push the captain’s left and right brake pedals until the brake force gage at each pedal
shows the value in Table 1.
(e) Hold the brake pedals in this position.
(f) Make sure that the hydraulic pressure at each brake is within the specified pressure.
(g) Make sure that the angle of the captain’s left and right brake pedals are 4.5 ± 1.5
degrees.
(h) Release the captain’s brake pedals.
(i) Make sure that the brakes fully release by observing that the brake pistons retract away
from the heat sink.
(j) Make sure that the angle of the captain's left and right brake pedals are 0.0 ± 0.50
degrees.
(k) Push the captain’s brake pedals fully down. Make sure that the hydraulic pressure at
each brake is 3000 ±150 psi (20,684 ±1034 kPa).
(l) Release the captain’s brake pedals.
(m) Make sure that the brakes fully release by observing that the brake pistons retract away
from the brake heat sink.
(n) Repeat the steps (1)(a) through (1)(l) using the first officer’s brake pedals.
(o) For the A or the B hydraulic systems, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power
Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805.

NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. General
(1) This task has instructions to test the operation of the brake accumulator system. This will test
the operation of the accumulator charging valve, the pressure transmitter, the accumulator
isolation valve, and the accumulator pressure gauge.

SUBTASK 32-41-00-790-006
(4) Do these steps that follow to do an operational test of the alternate (System A) brake system:
WARNING
KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL
SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR.
THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY
HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(a) For the system A (alternate), do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization,
TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
NOTE: At least one person needs to be stationed near the main landing gear brakes.
1) Repeat brake pedal application and release as needed to verify operation of each
brake.
(b) Fully push the captain's brake pedals.
(c) Observe the movement of each brake’s pistons or wear pins to make sure that the brakes
engaged.

SUBTASK 32-41-11-420-004
(1) If it is necessary, install the elbow fitting [9] to the hose half [1] of the quick disconnect:
(a) Apply a thin layer of hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the elbow threads of the hose half [1] of
the quick disconnect.
(b) Install the elbow fitting [9] to the hose half [1] of the quick disconnect.
(c) Do not tighten the B-nut on the hose half [1] of the quick disconnect at this time.
SUBTASK 32-41-11-420-001
(2) Brake Disconnect Installation (Hose Half):
(a) Remove the cap/plug, STD-14686, from the hydraulic hose [8].
(b) Apply a thin layer of hydraulic fluid, D00153, to the hydraulic hose [8] threads and elbow
fitting [9] threads.
(c) Connect the hydraulic hose [8] to the elbow fitting [9], do not tighten at this time.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(d) If it is necessary, loosen the B-nut of the hose half [1] of the quick disconnect.
(e) Turn the elbow fitting [9] on the hose half [1] of the quick disconnect. Make sure that it is
parallel to the oleo centerline or a maximum of ten degrees to the oleo centerline (away
from the tire).
CAUTION
USE TWO WRENCHES TO TORQUE THE HOSE B-NUT. USE ONE TO
HOLD THE ELBOW FITTING, AND THE OTHER TO TORQUE THE HOSE
B-NUT. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN
OCCUR.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU DO NOT TWIST OR MAKE KINKS IN THE HOSE
WHEN YOU TIGHTEN THE NUT. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO
THE EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(f) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic hose [8].
1) Apply initial torque to 270 ±14 in-lb (31 ±2 N·m).
2) Loosen the B-nut on the hydraulic hose [8] to decrease the torque to zero.
3) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic hose [8] to 400 ±20 in-lb (45 ±2 N·m).
(g) Tighten the B-nut on the elbow fitting [9] connection to hose half [1] quick disconnect.
1) Apply initial torque to 270 ±14 in-lb (31 ±2 N·m).
2) Loosen the B-nut on the hose half [1] of the quick disconnect to decrease the torque
to zero.
3) Tighten the B-nut on the hose half [1] of the quick disconnect to 400 ±20 in-lb
(45 ±2 N·m).
(h) Apply torque stripes, G50411, or other special identification mark to the B-nuts.
SUBTASK 32-41-11-420-002
(3) Brake Disconnect Installation (Brake Half):
(a) Lubricate the new packing [6] and the two new rings [5] with hydraulic fluid, D00153.
(b) Install the new packing [6] and the two new rings [5] on the brake half [7] of the quick
disconnect.
(c) Apply a thin layer of BATCO X8401-2 grease, D00571, to the brake half [7] of the
disconnect.
(d) Make sure that the BATCO X8401-2 grease, D00571, is on the diametral surface above
the upper retaining ring and the lower surface of the mounting flange.
(e) Install the brake half [7] of the quick disconnect on the brake.
1) Make sure that the alignment pin on the brake goes into the alignment hole in the
brake half [7] of the quick disconnect.
(f) Apply the BATCO X8401-2 grease, D00571, to the bolts [3].
(g) Install the bolts [3] and washers [4] that hold the brake half [7] of the quick disconnect to
the brake.
(h) Tighten the bolts [3] to 72 in-lb (8 N·m) - 82 in-lb (9 N·m).
(i) Install MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, or Safety Cable, G50466, on the bolts [3] in pairs.
(j) Make sure that the MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, or Safety Cable, G50466, passes
through the lug hole to the other bolt head on each side of the disconnect (Figure 401).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 32-41-11-420-003
(4) Install the hose half [1] of the quick disconnect to the brake half [7] of the quick disconnect on
the brake.
(a) Install the hose half [1] on the brake half [7].
1) Turn the hose half [1] until the internal tangs align with the slots inside the brake
half [7] and you can push the hose half down.
2) Push down on the barrel [2] and turn it clockwise to engage the threads.
3) Turn the barrel [2] clockwise until the lock in the bottom of the barrel [2] snaps onto
the external lock on the brake half [7].
4) Make sure that the elbow fitting [9] is ten degrees from parallel to the oleo centerline
towards the shock strut.
NOTE: This is to help prevent worn areas on the hoses.
(b) Do a visual check to make sure that the lock on hose half [1] is fully and correctly
engaged with the lock on the brake half [7].

E. Brake Pedal Bus Crank Assembly Removal
SUBTASK 32-41-22-020-001
(1) Remove the brake control cables [21] from the brake pedal bus crank assembly [1]
(TASK 32-41-81-000-801).
SUBTASK 32-41-22-020-002
(2) Disconnect the aft ends of the rod assemblies [7] from the bellcrank assemblies [6]
(TASK 27-21-31-000-801).
SUBTASK 32-41-22-020-003
(3) Remove the bolts [2], bushings [3], washers [4], and nuts [5] to disconnect the rod
assemblies [8] from the crank assembly [9] and crank assembly [11].
SUBTASK 32-41-22-000-001
(4) On the right side only, remove the screws [12] and washers [13] to disconnect the bracket
assembly [36] from the brake pedal bus crank assembly [1].
SUBTASK 32-41-22-020-004
(5) Remove the bolts [14], washers [15], washers [16], and nuts [17] to remove the brake pedal
bus crank assembly [1] from the structure.
SUBTASK 32-41-22-020-005
(6) Remove the bolts [2], bushings [3], washers [4], and nuts [5] to remove the brake control rod
assemblies [7] from the crank assembly [9] and crank [10].
SUBTASK 32-41-22-020-006
(7) Disassemble the brake pedal bus crank assembly [1].
(a) Remove the bolt [18], washer [19], and nut [20] from the crank [10].
(b) Remove the pin [22], nut [23], if installed washer [24], and spacer [25] from the shaft [31].
1) Discard the pin [22].
(c) Remove the pin [22], nut [35], if installed washer [34], and washer [33] from the shaft [31].
1) Discard the pin [22].
(d) Remove the shaft [31], bearing [26], crank assembly [11], bearing [27], spacer [28], crank
assembly [9], crank [10], and spacer [30] from the bus support assembly [37].
1) If necessary for the replacement, remove the bearing [32] from the bus support
assembly [37].
2) If necessary for the replacement, remove the bearing [29] from the crank
assembly [9].

F. Brake Pedal Bus Crank Assembly Installation
SUBTASK 32-41-22-420-001
(1) If removed for the replacement, install new bearing [32] and new bearing [29] as follows:
(a) Apply coating, G50961 to the bearing [32]. Roller swage to the bus support assembly [37]
(Bearings and Bushings - Removal/Installation, TASK 20-10-02-900-801).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) Apply coating, G50961 to the bearing [29]. Roller swage to the crank assembly [9]
(Bearings and Bushings - Removal/Installation, TASK 20-10-02-900-801).
SUBTASK 32-41-22-420-010
(2) Install the shaft [31] to the bus support assembly [37] as follows:
(a) Install the spacer [30] onto the shaft [31]. Install shaft [31] into the crank [10] and the bus
support assembly [37] with the washer [33] and, if removed, washer [34].
(b) Apply Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 to the nut [35]. Install the nut [35] to the
shaft [31].
1) Tighten the nut [35] 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m) - 100 in-lb (11.3 N·m).
(c) Install new pin [22] to nut [35].
(d) Install the crank assembly [9] and spacer [28] to the shaft [31].
(e) Apply AeroShell Grease 33, D50180 to bearing [26] and bearing [27].
(f) Install bearing [27], crank assembly [11], bearing [26], spacer [25], and, if removed,
washer [24] to shaft [31].
(g) Apply Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 to nut [23] and install to shaft [31].
1) Tighten the nut [23] 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m) - 100 in-lb (11.3 N·m).
(h) Install new pin [22] to the nut [23].
(i) Apply Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 to the bolt [18]. Install the bolt [18], washer [19],
and nut [20] to the crank [10].
1) Tighten the nut [20] 20 in-lb (2.3 N·m) above running torque.
SUBTASK 32-41-22-820-001
(3) Make sure that the clearance between the crank [10] and bus support assembly [37] is
0.015 in. (0.38 mm) - 0.050 in. (1.27 mm) (View A-A, Figure 401).
SUBTASK 32-41-22-420-002
(4) Attach the forward end of one rod assembly [7] to the short arm of the crank assembly [9].
Attach the other rod assembly [7] to the crank [10]. Install with the bolts [2], bushings [3],
washers [4], and nuts [5] to attach the rod assemblies [7].
SUBTASK 32-41-22-420-003
(5) Put the brake pedal bus crank assembly [1] into the structure. Install with the bolts [14],
washers [15], washers [16], and nuts [17].
NOTE: Install the washers [15] with the countersunk adjacent to the heads of the bolts [14].
SUBTASK 32-41-22-420-006
(6) On the right side only, install the screws [12] and washers [13] to connect the bracket
assembly [36] to the brake pedal bus crank assembly [1].
SUBTASK 32-41-22-420-007
(7) Install the rod assemblies [8] to the crank assembly [9] and crank assembly [11] using the
bolts [2], bushings [3], washers [4], and nuts [5].
SUBTASK 32-41-22-420-008
(8) Connect the aft ends of the rod assemblies [7] to the bellcrank assemblies [6]
(TASK 27-21-31-400-801).
SUBTASK 32-41-22-420-009
(9) Install the brake control cables [21] to the brake pedal bus crank assembly [1]
(TASK 32-41-81-400-801).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 32-41-22-820-002
(10) Do this task: Hydraulic Brake System - Adjustment, TASK 32-41-00-820-801.
SUBTASK 32-41-22-710-001
(11) Do this task: Normal and Alternate Brake Application - Functional Test,
TASK 32-41-00-710-801.

(10) Install the bolt [8], washer [9], and nut [10] to hold the crank to the shaft [11] on the brake
metering valve [1].
(a) For the right brake metering valve [1], make sure that the head of the bolt [8] points aft.
(b) For the left brake metering valve [1], make sure that the head of the bolt [8] points
forward.
SUBTASK 32-41-31-820-001
(11) Make sure that the rig pin LGB3 or LGB4 moves freely through the rig pin hole.
(a) If you cannot move the rig pin freely, adjust the brake metering valve, do this task:
Hydraulic Brake System - Adjustment, TASK 32-41-00-820-801.
SUBTASK 32-41-31-080-003
(12) Remove the rig pin LGB3 or LGB4.
SUBTASK 32-41-31-080-002
(13) Remove the plugs from the hydraulic lines.
SUBTASK 32-41-31-420-005
(14) Connect the hydraulic lines [32] to the brake metering valve [1].
NOTE: Each port on the metering valve may have a marking of the designated hydraulic
system, and it may not correspond to the hydraulic system used on the aircraft. Refer
to Figure 401 for the correct connection.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 32-41-31-420-008
(15) Tighten the B-nuts on the hydraulic lines [32] to 170.0 ±8.5 in-lb (19.2 ±1.0 N·m).
SUBTASK 32-41-31-420-009
(16) Connect the hydraulic lines [33] to the brake metering valve [1].
SUBTASK 32-41-31-420-010
(17) Tighten the B-nuts on the hydraulic lines [33] to 140.0 ±7.0 in-lb (15.8 ±0.8 N·m).
SUBTASK 32-41-31-420-011
(18) Connect the hydraulic line [34], hydraulic line [35], hydraulic line [36], hydraulic line [37], and
hydraulic line [38] to the brake metering valve [1].
SUBTASK 32-41-31-420-012
(19) Tighten the B-nuts on the hydraulic line [34], hydraulic line [35], hydraulic line [36], and
hydraulic line [37] to 270.0 ±13.5 in-lb (30.5 ±1.5 N·m).
SUBTASK 32-41-31-420-016
(20) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [38] to 170.0 ±8.5 in-lb (19.2 ±1.0 N·m).
SUBTASK 32-41-31-640-001
(21) Lubricate the two control rod end bearings [31] with grease, D00633.
G. Brake Metering Valve Installation Test
SUBTASK 32-41-31-790-001
(1) Do a leak check and operational check of the brake metering valve for each hydraulic system,
do these steps:
(a) For the normal (System B) hydraulic system:
WARNING
MAKE SURE ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE
FLIGHT CONTROLS SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND
THE LANDING GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE
SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN
CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
1) Do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
2) Fully push the captain's brake pedals twelve times.
3) Make sure that there are no leaks around the brake metering valve.
4) Check the brake wear indicators on the brakes to make sure that the brakes
engaged.
(b) For the alternate (System A) hydraulic system:
WARNING
MAKE SURE ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE
FLIGHT CONTROLS SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND
THE LANDING GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE
SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN
CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
1) Do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
2) Fully push the captain's brake pedals twelve times.
3) Make sure that there are no leaks around the brake metering valve.
4) Check the brake wear indicators on the brakes to make sure that the brakes
engaged.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 32-41-31-790-002
(2) Do a gear retract braking actuator check:
WARNING
MAKE SURE ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE
FLIGHT CONTROLS SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE
LANDING GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN
YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO
PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(a) For the normal (System B) and the alternate (System A) hydraulic system, do this task:
Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE
LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING
GEAR CAN RETRACT. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS, AND
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(b) Move the control lever for the landing gear to the UP position.
NOTE: Each gear door connects to each shock strut and only moves when that landing
gear extends or retracts.
(c) Check the brake wear indicators on the brakes to make sure that the brakes engaged.
(d) Make sure that the valve assembly does not produce noise or unusual sound.
(e) Make sure that there are no leaks around the brake metering valve.
(f) Move the control lever for the landing gear to the DN position.
(g) Check each brake’s pistons to make sure that all brakes are released.
SUBTASK 32-41-31-710-001
(3) For each hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal,
TASK 29-11-00-860-805.
SUBTASK 32-41-31-710-002

(b) For the alternate brake metering valves, do this task: Hydraulic Brake System - Bleeding

SUBTASK 32-41-41-420-012
CAUTION
BE VERY CAREFUL WHEN YOU DO MAINTENANCE ON CARBON BRAKES.
CARBON BRAKES ARE MORE EASILY DAMAGED THAN STEEL BRAKES.
YOU CAN NOT REPAIR THEM. IF YOU LET THEM FALL OR HIT THEM,
DAMAGE CAN OCCUR.
CAUTION
DO NOT APPLY FORCE TO THE CARBON BRAKE HEAT SHIELDS WHEN
YOU REMOVE OR INSTALL THE CARBON BRAKES. BENT HEAT SHIELDS
CANNOT BE REPAIRED. A CARBON BRAKE WITH A BENT HEAT SHIELD
WILL CAUSE SCORING ON THE WHEEL INNER SURFACE WHEN THE
WHEEL TURNS.
CAUTION
DO NOT PUT THE BRAKE DOWN ON THE OUTER DIAMETER OF THE
ROTORS AFTER YOU REMOVE IT. CARBON BRAKES ARE NOT
SERVICEABLE IF THEY HAVE NICKS, OR CRACKS. YOU CANNOT REPAIR
THEM. THE WEIGHT OF THE BRAKE CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO CARBON
BRAKE ROTORS.

1) Turn the hose half of the brake disconnect [3] until the internal tangs align with the
slots inside the brake half of the brake disconnect [3] and you can push the hose
half down.
2) Push down on the barrel and turn it clockwise to engage the threads.
3) Turn the barrel clockwise until the slots in the bottom of the barrel snap onto the
external tangs on the brake half of the brake disconnect [3].

centerline or up to ten degrees toward the shock strut to avoid hoses rubbing on the
brake housing.

I. Main Gear Wheel Brakes Bleeding and Installation Test
SUBTASK 32-41-41-860-011
WARNING
KEEP PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE FLIGHT CONTROL
SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE
COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC
POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(1) For the normal (System B) hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B
Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
SUBTASK 32-41-41-790-005
(2) Do these steps to do an operational check of all four brakes:
NOTE: At least one person needs to be stationed near the main landing gear brakes. Repeat
brake pedal application and release as needed to verify operation of each brake.
(a) Push one set of brake pedals to the limit of travel to fully operate each brake assy [1].
(b) Set the parking brake.
(c) Monitor the movement of each brake's pistons or wear pins to make sure that each brake
assy [1] engaged.
NOTE: If the brake wear pins move, the brakes will engage.
(d) Wait two minutes.
(e) Look for leaks around each brake assy [1] and at each brake disconnect [3].
(f) Release the parking brake.
(g) Monitor the movement of each brake's pistons or wear pins to make sure that each brake
assy [1] released.
NOTE: If the brake wear pins move, the brakes will release.
SUBTASK 32-41-41-870-002
(3) If the brakes do not feel normal, do this task: Normal (System B) Hydraulic Brake System -
Bleeding, TASK 32-41-00-870-802.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

(a) With the brake released, visually check to make sure that there is clearance between

(b) Make sure that the running clearance between each brake piston and pressure plate is

(c) If the running clearance is less than 0.050 in. (1.270 mm), replace the main landing gear

(6) Check the visible areas of the brake heat sink (rotors, stators, pressure plate, and end plate)

(a) Replace the carbon brakes if these conditions exist (Figure 604 or Figure 605 or

1) Examine the brakes for indentations or flaking carbon where the hydraulic brake
pistons touch the carbon pressure plate.
2) Examine the brake and surrounding areas for unusual carbon debris such as chips
or small pieces of carbon broken off of the rotors and stators.
3) Make sure that the metal rotor drive clips on the outside diameter of each carbon
rotor do not show excessive movement and there is no loose flaking carbon near
the clips.
(b) Do a check for loose rotor drive clips and rivets.
(c) Do a check for pieces of carbon that have broken off the carbon disks.
(d) Do a check of the outside diameter of the stator disks for the correct 12 o’clock positions
of their alignment grooves (Figure 604 or Figure 605 or Figure 606).
NOTE: Most carbon brakes are configured with worn stator indicators. A worn stator
indicator is a line machined in the stator at the 12 o’clock position of the heatsink.
If this indicator is available on the heatsink, the indicator can be used as a visual
reference to make sure that the stator does not rotate more than 0.25 in.
(0.64 cm).
NOTE: A stator groove that is not aligned is an indication of possible stator disk drive
failure.
NOTE: Manufacturing of alignment markings vary from brake supplier to brake supplier,
not all brake assemblies have this indicator.
1) With one hand at the 3 o’clock position and the other hand at the 9 o’clock position,
rotate each stator individually and see that the stator does not move more than
0.25 in. (0.64 cm) as measured on the outside diameter of the adjacent stators.
2) Replace the brake if any of the stators can be moved by hand beyond 0.25 in.
(0.64 cm).

 ALL

rotors and stators. Stains that are brown or orange are initial indications of
possible oxidation. Oxidation damage normally occurs on the outside diameters
of rotors and stators and non-wear surfaces of pressure plate and end plate and
is easy to see. Oxidation damage can also occur on the inner diameter of the
rotors and stators, end plate and pressure plate.

F. Brake Accumulator Installation
SUBTASK 32-41-51-020-003
(1) Remove the caps or plugs from the ports of the brake accumulator [1].
SUBTASK 32-41-51-410-001
(2) If the reducer [3] and reducer [5] are not installed in the brake accumulator [1], do these steps:
(a) Lubricate the new packing [2], new packing [4], reducer [3], and reducer [5] with hydraulic
fluid, D00153, or MCS 352B fluid, D00054.
(b) For the GAS end of the brake accumulator [1]:
1) Install the new packing [2] on the reducer [3].
2) Install the reducer [3] in the GAS PORT of the brake accumulator [1].
3) Tighten the reducer [3] to 180 in-lb (20.34 N·m) - 200 in-lb (22.60 N·m).
(c) For the HYDRAULIC end of the brake accumulator [1]:
1) Install the new packing [4] on the reducer [5].
2) Install the reducer [5] in the FLUID PORT of the brake accumulator [1].
3) Tighten the reducer [5] to 855 in-lb (96.60 N·m) - 945 in-lb (106.77 N·m).
SUBTASK 32-41-51-420-001
(3) Do the steps that follow to install the brake accumulator [1]:
(a) Align the gas line with the reducer [3] on the brake accumulator [1] when you put the
brake accumulator [1] in its position in the clamps.
(b) Tighten the clamp nuts.
(c) Connect the gas line from the charging valve [8] to the GAS PORT of the brake
accumulator [1].
(d) Connect the hydraulic line to the FLUID PORT of the brake accumulator [1].
SUBTASK 32-41-51-420-002
(4) Do the steps that follow to put the brake accumulator [1] back to its usual condition:
(a) Do this task: Hydraulic Brake Accumulator Servicing, TASK 12-15-11-420-801.
1) Make sure that the cap [6] is installed on the charging valve [8] and it has lockwire,
G01505 (TASK 20-10-44-400-801).
WARNING
KEEP PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT
CONTROL SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING
GEAR. THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU
SUPPLY HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO
PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(b) For the normal (System B) hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B
Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
(c) Make sure that the gages for normal (System B) hydraulic system and the brake
accumulator [1] indicate approximately 3000 psig (3000 psi).
(d) Make sure that there is no leak at the connection for the hydraulic line on the brake
accumulator [1].
(e) Apply a soap solution to the connection at the charging line.
1) Examine the connection for air bubbles.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(f) If leakage is detected at the charging valve [8], do the following steps to remove and
replace the charging valve [8]:
1) Make sure that the hydraulic reservoirs have been depressurized before you
remove the charging valve [8] (TASK 29-09-00-860-802).
2) Remove the cap [6] on the charging valve [8] then slowly unscrew the swivel nut [7]
to release any residual air pressure.
3) Remove lockwire from the charging valve [8] and manifold assembly.
4) Remove the charging valve [8] from the manifold assembly.
5) Remove and discard the packing [20] from the charging valve [8].
6) Lubricate the new packing [20] with MCS 352B fluid, D00054, or hydraulic fluid,
D00153.
7) Install the new packing [20] onto the charging valve [8].
8) Install the charging valve [8] in manifold assembly port.
a) Tighten the charging valve [8] to 100 in-lb (11 N·m) - 110 in-lb (12 N·m).
9) Install MS20995C47 lockwire, G50356, to the charging valve [8] and manifold
assembly with the double twist method.
10) Install the cap [6] and tighten swivel nut [7] on the charging valve [8].
11) Pressurize the pneumatic crossover manifold duct.
12) Use a solution of soap and water to make sure that no air leaks are at the charging
valve [8].
13) Release pressure from the pneumatic cross manifold duct.
(g) To bleed the normal (System B) hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic Brake System -
Bleeding Upstream of the Antiskid Valves, TASK 32-41-00-870-801.

Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or Hydraulic Reservoirs
Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-808.
(b) Push and release the brake pedals fully a minimum of seven times.
(c) Monitor the movement of the brake-wear indicators on each brake to make sure that the

CAN RETRACT. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS, AND DAMAGE
TO EQUIPMENT.

Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801.

PAGEBLOCK 10-11-05/201).

TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-808.

(4) Release the parking brake.
SUBTASK 32-41-51-860-006

brake accumulator.
SUBTASK 32-41-51-840-001
(6) Do these steps to remove the gas pressure from the brake accumulator:
(a) Remove the cap [6] from the brake accumulator charging valve [8].
WARNING
DO NOT LET THE VALVE TURN WITH THE SWIVEL NUT. THE
PRESSURE IN THE ACCUMULATOR WILL DISENGAGE THE VALVE
WITH EXPLOSIVE FORCE. INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE
TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(b) Loosen the swivel nut [7] on the charging valve [8] a maximum of one complete turn
counter-clockwise to release the gas pressure from the brake accumulator [1].
(c) Make sure that the gage assembly [9] for the brake accumulator goes to zero.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 32-41-51-020-004

(a) Disconnect the gas line [10] from the gage assembly [9].
(b) Install a plug on the gas line [10].
(c) Remove the screws [11], washers [12], washers [13], and washers [14] from the airplane.
(d) Remove the shield [16] from the airplane.
(e) Remove the washers [13], washers [14], and spacers [15].
(f) Remove the gage assembly [9] from the airplane.
1) Remove the flange [18] from the gage assembly [9].
(g) Put a cap on the union [19] on the gage.

WARNING
KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL
SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR.
THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY

pedals.

Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805.

G. Hydraulic Brake Control Cable Removal
NOTE: The steps that follow are applicable for all of the brake control cables.
SUBTASK 32-41-81-020-001
(1) In the forward compartment, forward of the nose wheel well, do these steps:
(a) Install a control cable clamp, SPL-1569, on the cable (aft cable [2] or forward cable [4])
opposite the one you will remove to keep light tension on the cable (aft cable [2] or
forward cable [4]).
NOTE: Light tension on the aft cable or forward cable will prevent wind off on the cable
drums. Light tension will also make sure that the cables do not move out of the
quadrant guides.
(b) Remove the locking clip [1] from the turnbuckle [3] on the aft cable [2], forward cable [4]
(TASK 20-10-10-000-801).
(c) Loosen the turnbuckle [3] for the aft cable [2], forward cable [4] to release the tension in
the cable.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Make sure that you keep light tension on the aft cable [2] or forward cable [4] to
keep the aft cable [2] or forward cable [4] in the quadrant [5] or quadrant [8] guides.
(d) Disconnect the forward cable [4] from the quadrant [5]:
1) Remove the pin [7], that holds the end of the forward cable [4], from the
quadrant [5].
2) Pull the fitting on the end of the control forward cable [4] from the control
quadrant [5].
3) Remove the forward cable [4] from the quadrant [5].
SUBTASK 32-41-81-020-002
(2) In the passenger compartment, do these steps:
(a) Disconnect the brake control aft cable [2] from the quadrant [8]:
1) Remove the pin [9], that holds the end of the aft cable [2], from the quadrant [8].
2) Pull the fitting on the end of the control aft cable [2] from the control quadrant [8].
SUBTASK 32-41-81-020-003
(3) Attach the new aft cable [2] or forward cable [4], or a piece of string, STD-837, to the old aft
cable [2].
NOTE: The new aft cable or forward cable must be pulled through the system to make the
new aft cable or forward cable installation easy. If you remove the old aft cable or
forward cable without attaching anything to it, installation of the new aft cable or
forward cable will be very difficult.
SUBTASK 32-41-81-020-004
(4) Remove the aft cable [2] or forward cable [4]:
(a) Pull the old aft cable [2] or forward cable [4] out, that will pull the new aft cable [2] or
forward cable [4], or string, STD-837, through the cable system at the same time.
1) Make sure that the new aft cable [2] or forward cable [4] has grease, D00633,
applied to it before it is installed.

D. Brake Accumulator Isolation Valve Removal
SUBTASK 32-41-91-020-001
(1) Do these steps to remove the accumulator isolation valve [13]:
(a) Disconnect the hydraulic line [1], hydraulic line [8], and elbow [11] from the accumulator
isolation valve [13].
(b) Install the plugs in the hydraulic line [1], hydraulic line [8], and elbow [11].
(c) Install the caps on the reducer [2], reducer [7], and reducer [10] in the ports of the
accumulator isolation valve [13].
(d) Remove the bolts [4] and washers [5] that attach the accumulator isolation valve [13] to
the mating surface.
(e) Remove the accumulator isolation valve [13] from the airplane.
SUBTASK 32-41-91-020-002
(2) If the replacement accumulator isolation valve [13] does not have hydraulic fittings installed, do
these steps:
(a) Remove the reducer [2], reducer [7], reducer [10], and plugs [14] from the ports of the
accumulator isolation valve [13].
1) Remove the lockwire from the plugs [14].
(b) Remove and discard the packing [6], packing [9], and packings [3].
(c) Install plugs in the hydraulic ports of the accumulator isolation valve [13].

E. Prepare for the Installation
SUBTASK 32-41-91-110-001
(1) Prepare the mating surfaces for installation of the accumulator isolation valve [13] (Figure 401).
(a) Clean the mating surface of the accumulator isolation valve [13] with solvent, B00083.

F. Brake Accumulator Isolation Valve Installation
SUBTASK 32-41-91-640-001
(1) If the reducer [2], reducer [7], reducer [10], plugs [14], packings [3], packing [6], and
packing [9] are not installed, do these steps:
(a) Lubricate the reducer [2], reducer [7], reducer [10], plugs [14], new packings [3], new
packing [6], and new packing [9] with hydraulic fluid, D00153, or MCS 352B fluid,
D00054.
(b) Install the reducer [2], reducer [7], reducer [10], plugs [14], packings [3], packing [6], and
packing [9] in their location on the accumulator isolation valve [13].
 ALL; BRAKE ACCUMULATOR ISOLATION VALVE WITH PLUG P/N 274T4629-1
1) Tighten the reducer [2] to 270 ±14 in-lb (30.5 ±1.6 N·m).
NOTE: The reducer is made of steel.
 ALL; BRAKE ACCUMULATOR ISOLATION VALVE WITH PLUG P/N 274T4629-4
2) Tighten the reducer [2] to 170 ±9 in-lb (19.2 ±1.0 N·m).
NOTE: The reducer is made of aluminum alloy.
 ALL
3) Tighten the reducer [7] to 280 ±14 in-lb (31.6 ±1.6 N·m).
4) Tighten the reducer [10] to 280 ±14 in-lb (31.6 ±1.6 N·m).
(c) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G50347, on the plugs [14] with the double-twist method.
SUBTASK 32-41-91-420-001
(2) Do these steps to install the accumulator isolation valve [13]:
(a) Put the accumulator isolation valve [13] on the mating surface.
(b) Install the bolts [4] and washers [5] to attach the accumulator isolation valve [13] on the
mating surface.
(c) Remove the caps from the hydraulic ports of the accumulator isolation valve [13].
(d) Remove the plugs from the hydraulic line [1], hydraulic line [8], and elbow [11].
(e) Connect the hydraulic line [1], hydraulic line [8], and elbow [11] to the accumulator
isolation valve [13].
1) Tighten the hydraulic line [1] to 140 ±7 in-lb (15.8 ±0.8 N·m).
2) Tighten the hydraulic line [8] to 270 ±14 in-lb (30.5 ±1.6 N·m).
3) Tighten the elbow [11] to 270 ±14 in-lb (30.5 ±1.6 N·m).

SUBTASK 32-41-91-870-003
(1) Do the steps that follow to make sure that the valve assembly does not leak:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
WARNING
KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL
SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR.
THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY
HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.

accumulator isolation valve [13] do not leak.
SUBTASK 32-41-91-870-002
(2) Bleed the brake hydraulic system:
(a) Operate the brake pedals 6 times.
NOTE: Operate the pedals slowly and wait a minimum of 5 seconds between each time

SUBTASK 32-41-91-840-002
(4) Set the parking brakes.
SUBTASK 32-41-91-840-003

D. Alternate Brake Selector Valve Removal
SUBTASK 32-41-93-020-001
(1) Do these steps to remove the alternate brake selector valve [1]:
(a) Disconnect the electrical connector [3] from the pressure switch [2] on the alternate brake
selector valve [1].
(b) Disconnect the hydraulic line [6] from the normal port on the alternate brake selector
valve [1].
(c) Disconnect the T-fitting [7] from the return port on the alternate brake selector valve [1].
(d) Disconnect the T-fitting [10] from the brake port on the alternate brake selector valve [1].
(e) Disconnect the elbow [13] from the alt pressure port on the alternate brake selector
valve [1].
(f) Install caps on the hydraulic line [6], T-fitting [7], T-fitting [10], and elbow [13].
(g) Install plugs in the hydraulic ports of the alternate brake selector valve [1].
(h) Remove the nuts [16] and washers [17] that attach the alternate brake selector valve [1]
to the mating surface.
(i) Remove the alternate brake selector valve [1] from the airplane.
SUBTASK 32-41-93-020-002
(2) If you will install a new alternate brake selector valve [1] without the unions or reducers, do
these steps:
(a) Remove the union [8], reducer [5], reducer [11], and reducer [14] from the alternate brake
selector valve [1].
(b) Remove and discard the packing [4], packing [9], packing [12], and packing [15].
SUBTASK 32-41-93-020-003
(3) Do the steps that follow to remove the pressure switch [2] from the alternate brake selector
valve [1]:
(a) Remove and discard the lockwire from the pressure switch [2] and alternate brake
selector valve [1].
(b) Remove the pressure switch [2] from the alternate brake selector valve [1].
(c) Remove and discard the packing [18] from the pressure switch [2].

SUBTASK 32-41-93-640-001
(1) If the union, reducers, and packings are not installed, do these steps:

packing [9], new packing [12], new packing [15] with hydraulic fluid, D00153, or MCS
352B fluid, D00054.

 ALL; ALTERNATE BRAKE SELECTOR VALVE WITH PLUG P/N 274T4629-1

 ALL
3) Tighten the reducer [11] to 280 ±14 in-lb (31.6 ±1.6 N·m).

 ALL
SUBTASK 32-41-93-420-001

steps:

(c) Remove the plugs from the hydraulic ports of the alternate brake selector valve [1].
(d) Remove the caps from the hydraulic line [6], T-fitting [7], T-fitting [10], and elbow [13].
(e) Connect the hydraulic line [6] to the normal port on the alternate brake selector valve [1].
1) Tighten the B-nut on the hydraulic line [6] to 140 ±7 in-lb (15.8 ±0.8 N·m).

1) Tighten the B-nut on the T-fitting [10] to 270 ±14 in-lb (30.5 ±1.6 N·m).
(h) Connect the elbow [13] to the alt pressure port on the alternate brake selector valve [1].
1) Tighten the B-nut on the elbow [13] to 270 ±14 in-lb (30.5 ±1.6 N·m).

brake selector valve [1], examine the connector for corrosion.

WARNING

(1) If the downlock pins are not installed in the nose and main landing gear, do this task: Landing
Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801.
SUBTASK 32-41-93-860-019

E. Gear Retract Braking Operational Test
SUBTASK 32-41-93-480-011
(1) Do these steps to install a pressure gage at each brake:
(a) Disconnect the brake at the brake disconnect:
1) Push the barrel toward the brake and rotate the barrel clockwise to disengage the
brake half from the hose half.
2) Pull up on the barrel of the brake disconnect away from the brake until the threads
of the two halves are engaged.
3) Turn the barrel counterclockwise to disconnect the brake hose from the brake
assembly.
(b) Remove the brake bleeder assembly from the brake.
NOTE: Each brake bleeder assembly has a bleeder valve installed in an adapter. The
adapter is installed in the brake.
(c) Install the pressure gauge, SPL-15031, or optional gauge set, SPL-10813, or gauge set,
SPL-1819.
(d) Connect the brake at the brake disconnect:
1) Turn the hose half of the brake disconnect until the internal tangs align with the slots
inside the brake half of the brake disconnect and you can push the hose half down.
2) Push down on the barrel and turn it clockwise to engage the threads.
3) Turn the barrel clockwise until the slots in the bottom of the barrel snap into place
on the external tangs on the brake half of the brake disconnect.
(e) Do a visual check to make sure that the slots on the barrel are fully and correctly
engaged with the tangs on the brake half of the brake disconnect.
SUBTASK 32-41-93-790-003
WARNING
KEEP PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE FLIGHT CONTROL
SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE
COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC
POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(2) For the normal (system B) and alternate (system A) hydraulic systems, do this task: Hydraulic
System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 32-41-93-860-007
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED IN ALL OF THE
LANDING GEAR BEFORE YOU MOVE THE CONTROL LEVER. WITHOUT
THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR CAN RETRACT AND CAUSE
INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(3) Put the landing gear control lever in the UP position.
SUBTASK 32-41-93-870-003
(4) Wait 2 seconds.
SUBTASK 32-41-93-710-002
(5) Make sure that the hydraulic pressure at all brakes is 500 psig (3447 kPa) - 575 psig
(3964 kPa).
SUBTASK 32-41-93-710-003
(6) Put the landing gear control lever in the DOWN position.
SUBTASK 32-41-93-710-004
(7) Make sure that the hydraulic pressure at all of the brakes is less than 60 psig (414 kPa).
SUBTASK 32-41-93-860-020
(8) For the normal (system B) and alternate (system A) hydraulic systems, do this task: Hydraulic
Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-802.
SUBTASK 32-41-93-480-012
(9) Do these steps to remove the pressure gages at each brake:
(a) Disconnect the brake at the brake disconnect:
1) Pull up on the barrel of the brake disconnect.
2) Turn the barrel counterclockwise to disconnect the brake hose from the brake
assembly.
(b) Remove the pressure gauge, SPL-15031, or optional gauge set, SPL-10813, or gauge
set, SPL-1819.
(c) Install the brake bleeder assembly on the brake.
NOTE: Each brake bleeder assembly has a bleeder valve installed in an adapter. The
adapter is installed in the brake.
(d) Connect the brake at the brake disconnect:
1) Turn the hose half of the brake disconnect until the internal tangs align with the slots
inside the brake half of the brake disconnect and you can push the hose half down.
2) Push down on the barrel and turn it clockwise to engage the threads.
3) Turn the barrel clockwise until the slots in the bottom of the barrel snap into place
on the external tangs on the brake half of the brake disconnect.
(e) Do a visual check to make sure that the slots on the barrel are fully and correctly
engaged with the tangs on the brake half of the brake disconnect.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

D. Brake Shuttle Valve Removal
SUBTASK 32-41-95-020-001
(1) Do the steps that follow to remove the valve assembly [5]:

(c) Remove the bolts [3] or bolts [7] and washers [4].
(d) Remove the valve assembly [5] from the airplane.
SUBTASK 32-41-95-020-002
(2) If the valve assembly [5] you install does not have the unions [1] installed, do these steps:

E. Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit Operational Test
SUBTASK 32-42-00-860-008
(1) Do the following steps for AACU:
(a) Push and then release the RESET switch on the AACU.
(b) Make sure that the display on the front panel of the AACU shows MEM CLR and then
clears.
(c) Set the AUTOBRAKE selector switch on the P2-2 panel to "OFF" then to position "1".
NOTE: If the AUTOBRAKE DISARM light is on when you do three subsequent steps, the
test will not successfully complete and one or more faults will show on the front
panel of the AACU.
(d) Push and hold the ENABLE/VERIFY switch on the AACU.
(e) While you hold the ENABLE/VERIFY switch, push and hold the VERIFY switch on the
AACU.

(a) Disconnect the brake at the brake disconnect:
1) Push the barrel toward the brake and rotate the barrel clockwise to disengage the
brake half from the hose half.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
2) Pull up on the barrel of the brake disconnect away from the brake until the threads
of the two halves are engaged.
3) Turn the barrel counterclockwise to disconnect the brake hose from the brake
assembly.
(b) Remove the brake bleeder assembly from the brake.
NOTE: Each brake bleeder assembly has a bleeder valve installed in an adapter. The
adapter is installed in the brake.

(d) Connect the brake at the brake disconnect:
1) Turn the hose half of the brake disconnect until the internal tangs align with the slots
inside the brake half of the brake disconnect and you can push the hose half down.
2) Push down on the barrel and turn it clockwise to engage the threads.
3) Turn the barrel clockwise until the slots in the bottom of the barrel snap into place
on the external tangs on the brake half of the brake disconnect.

engaged with the tangs on the brake half of the brake disconnect.

E. Transducer Functional Test
SUBTASK 32-42-00-020-001
(1) Do these steps to remove the hubcap (Figure 503):
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) For an outboard wheel, turn the camlock fasteners 1/4-turn to disconnect the hubcap
fairing from the outboard hubcap.
(b) Remove and discard MS20995N32 lockwire, G50177, from the bolts of the outboard or
inboard hubcap.
(c) Remove the bolts and washers to disconnect the outboard or inboard hubcap from the
wheel.
(d) Remove the outboard or inboard hubcap from the wheel.
SUBTASK 32-42-00-860-025
(2) Install the spin up adapter, SPL-1831, in a drill.
SUBTASK 32-42-00-860-026
(3) Make sure that the hydraulic pressure at all brakes is equal to the system B pressure ±200 psi
(1379 kPa).
NOTE: This is to make sure that the antiskid system does not inadvertently release the
brakes.
SUBTASK 32-42-00-710-002
(4) Do these steps to test each wheel speed transducer:
NOTE: A minimum of one person must be near the main landing gear brakes.
WARNING
KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THRUST REVERSERS.
THE OPERATION OF THE WHEEL SPEED TRANSDUCER CAN CAUSE
AUTOMATIC OPERATION OF THE STANDBY HYDRAULIC PUMP AND
SUDDEN THRUST REVERSER MOVEMENTS. IF YOU DO NOT DO THIS,
INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(a) Use the spin up adapter, SPL-1831, and a variable speed drill to turn the wheel speed
transducer between 250 and 2200 Revolutions Per Minute (RPM).
NOTE: It is recommended to keep the wheel speed below 60 knots. If the aircraft is not
in this condition, the standby hydraulic pump can operate automatically.
(b) Visually make sure that the brake at the paired wheel is less than or equal to 150 psi
(1034 kPa) (Table 501).
NOTE: The wheels are numbered from the left to the right.
Table 501/32-42-00-993-804 ANTISKID TRANSDUCER PAIRED WHEELS
TRANSDUCER PAIRED WHEEL
1 4
2 3
3 2
4 1
(c) Stop the movement of the wheel speed transducer as quickly as possible.
(d) Visually make sure that the brake at the controlled wheel is less than or equal to 150 psi
(1034 kPa) (Table 502).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
Table 502/32-42-00-993-806 ANTISKID TRANSDUCER CONTROLLED WHEELS

1 1
2 2

(e) Wait 5 to 10 seconds.
(f) Make sure that the hydraulic pressure at all brakes is equal to the system B pressure
±200 psi (1379 kPa).
SUBTASK 32-42-00-420-001
CAUTION
DO NOT TIGHTEN THE HUBCAP BOLTS TOO MUCH. MAKE SURE THAT THE
HUBCAP IS IN THE CORRECT POSITION BEFORE YOU TIGHTEN THE
BOLTS. TOO MUCH TORQUE WILL CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE BOLTS AND
THE HUBCAP.

the dog in the wheel will connect when the hubcap is installed.
(b) Put the hubcap in its position on the wheel.
1) Visually make sure that the hubcap is flush with the wheel assembly.
2) Use a soft rubber mallet, STD-3906, to lightly tap the hubcap to make it flush.
(c) Install the bolts and washers to connect the hubcap to the wheel.
1) Tighten the bolts to 50 in-lb (6 N·m) - 80 in-lb (9 N·m).
(d) Install MS20995N32 lockwire, G50177, on the bolts with the double twist method
TASK 20-10-44-400-801).
(e) Do these steps for the outboard wheel:
1) Put the hubcap fairing on the hubcap.
2) Turn the camlock fasteners 1/4-turn to attach the hubcap fairing to the hubcap.

D. Normal Antiskid Valve Operational Test
SUBTASK 32-42-00-860-035
(1) Do these steps for each antiskid valve that you removed or test:
NOTE: One person must be at the Main Landing Gear (MLG) brakes to monitor the movement
of the brake pistons or wear pins. This is to make sure that the correct brake releases
and engages.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(a) Move the BRAKE TEST selector switch on the Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit (AACU) to
the wheel position for the brake valve that you test.
NOTE: See the top of the AACU for the brake number.
(b) Push and hold the ENABLE/VERIFY switch on the AACU.
(c) Push and hold the VERIFY switch on the AACU.
(d) Release the ENABLE/VERIFY and the VERIFY switches at the same time.
NOTE: The AACU display will show BRK X during the test, where X = the wheel number
selected by the BRAKE TEST selector switch.
(e) Observe the movement of the brake pistons or wear pins to make sure that the selected
brake releases and then applies again.
(f) Make sure that there are no fault codes on the AACU display.
(g) Move the BRAKE TEST selector switch to the NORM position.

mode.
(a) Align the ADIRS (TASK 34-21-00-820-802 or TASK 34-21-00-820-801).
SUBTASK 32-42-00-480-018
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED IN ALL OF THE
LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR

(5) Make sure that the downlock pins are installed in the nose and main landing gear
(PAGEBLOCK 32-00-01/201).

for the two Main Landing Gear (MLG).
SUBTASK 32-42-00-480-016
(9) Do these steps to install a pressure gage at each brake:
(a) Disconnect the brake at the brake disconnect:
1) Pull up on the barrel of the brake disconnect.
2) Turn the barrel counterclockwise to disconnect the brake hose from the brake
assembly.
(b) Remove the brake bleeder assembly from the brake.
NOTE: Each brake bleeder assembly has a bleeder valve installed in an adapter. The
adapter is installed in the brake.
(c) Install the pressure gauge on the brake bleed port.
(d) Connect the brake at the brake disconnect:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Turn the hose half of the brake disconnect until the internal tangs align with the slots
inside the brake half of the brake disconnect and you can push the hose half down.
2) Push down on the barrel and turn it clockwise to engage the threads.
3) Turn the barrel clockwise until the slots in the bottom of the barrel snap into place
on the external tangs on the brake half of the brake disconnect.
(e) Do a visual check to make sure that the slots on the barrel are fully and correctly
engaged with the tangs on the brake half of the brake disconnect.

EQUIPMENT.

(13) Do the steps that follow for AUTO BRAKE selector position 1.

(b) Push and then release the RESET switch on the AACU.

(c) Push and hold the ENABLE/VERIFY switch on the AACU.
(d) While you hold the ENABLE/VERIFY switch, push and hold the VERIFY switch on the

(h) Set the AUTO BRAKE selector switch, on the P2-2 panel, to the OFF position.

E. Transducer Operational Test
SUBTASK 32-42-00-020-002
(1) If the hubcap is installed, do these steps to remove the hubcap (Figure 503):
(a) For an outboard wheel, turn the camlock fasteners 1/4-turn to disconnect the hubcap
fairing from the outboard hubcap.
(b) Remove and discard MS20995N32 lockwire, G50177, from the bolts of the outboard or
inboard hubcap.
(c) Remove the bolts and washers to disconnect the outboard or inboard hubcap from the
wheel.
(d) Remove the outboard or inboard hubcap from the wheel.
SUBTASK 32-42-00-020-003
(2) Do the steps that follow to check the mechanical condition of the transducer and drive
coupling:
(a) Turn the transducer drive coupling while you do a check to make sure that you do not
have these conditions:
1) Free play in the bearing for the transducer drive coupling.
2) A drive shaft for the transducer drive coupling that is bent.
SUBTASK 32-42-00-860-075
(3) Install the spin up adapter, SPL-1831, in a drill.
SUBTASK 32-42-00-710-004
(4) Do these steps for each wheel speed transducer that you will test:
NOTE: One person must be at the Main Landing Gear (MLG) brakes to monitor the movement
of the brake pistons or wear pins. This is to make sure that the correct brake releases
and engages.
WARNING
KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THRUST REVERSERS.
THE OPERATION OF THE WHEEL SPEED TRANSDUCER CAN CAUSE
AUTOMATIC OPERATION OF THE STANDBY HYDRAULIC PUMP AND
SUDDEN THRUST REVERSER MOVEMENTS. IF YOU DO NOT DO THIS,
INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(a) Use the spin up adapter, SPL-1831, and a variable speed drill to turn the wheel speed
transducer between 250 and 2200 Revolutions Per Minute (RPM).
NOTE: We recommend that you keep the wheel speed below 60 knots. If the aircraft is
not in this condition, the standby hydraulic pump can operate automatically.
(b) Observe the movement of the brake pistons or wear pins to make sure that the brake at
the paired wheel releases (Table 503).
NOTE: The wheels are numbered from the left to the right.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
Table 503/32-42-00-993-805 ANTISKID TRANSDUCER PAIRED WHEELS
TRANSDUCER PAIRED WHEEL
1 4
2 3
3 2
4 1
(c) Stop the movement of the wheel speed transducer as quickly as possible.
(d) Observe the movement of the brake pistons or wear pins to make sure that the brake at
the controlled wheel releases momentarily and then reapplies again in 5 to 10 seconds
(Table 504).
Table 504/32-42-00-993-808 ANTISKID TRANSDUCER CONTROLLED WHEELS

1 1
2 2

SUBTASK 32-42-00-420-002
CAUTION
DO NOT TIGHTEN THE HUBCAP BOLTS TOO MUCH. MAKE SURE THAT THE
HUBCAP IS IN THE CORRECT POSITION BEFORE YOU TIGHTEN THE
BOLTS. TOO MUCH TORQUE WILL CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE BOLTS AND
THE HUBCAP.
(5) Do these steps to install the hubcap (Figure 503):
(a) Turn the antiskid transducer dog inside the wheel such that the drive on the hubcap and
the dog in the wheel will connect when the hubcap is installed.
(b) Put the hubcap in its position on the wheel.
1) Visually make sure that the hubcap is flush with the wheel assembly.
a) Use a soft rubber mallet, STD-3906, to lightly tap the hubcap to make it flush.
(c) Install the bolts and washers to connect the hubcap to the wheel.
1) Tighten the bolts to 50 in-lb (6 N·m) - 80 in-lb (9 N·m).
(d) Install MS20995N32 lockwire, G50177, on the bolts with double twist method
(TASK 20-10-44-400-801).
(e) Do these steps for the outboard wheel:
1) Put the hubcap fairing on the hubcap.
2) Turn the camlock fasteners 1/4-turn to attach the hubcap fairing to the hubcap.

F. Transducer Removal
SUBTASK 32-42-11-020-001
(1) Do these steps to remove the hubcap [3]:
(a) For an outboard wheel, turn the eight CAM-LOCs [4] fasteners 1/4 turn to disconnect the
outboard hubcap fairing [5] from the hubcap [3].
(b) Remove the three bolts [6] and the washers [7] to disconnect the hubcap [3] from the
wheel assembly [1].
(c) Remove the hubcap [3] from the wheel assembly [1].
SUBTASK 32-42-11-020-002
(2) Remove the nuts [8], washers [9], and bolts [10] that hold the support [11] to the axle.
SUBTASK 32-42-11-020-003
(3) Do these steps to remove the transducer [14]:
NOTE: The transducer is held inside of the support with a locknut [13].
(a) Remove the MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, from the locknut [13] .
(b) Remove the locknut [13] from the support [11] with locknut wrench set, SPL-1873.
(c) Remove the transducer [14] from the axle.
(d) Disconnect the electrical connector [12] from the transducer [14].
NOTE: Identify each electrical connector/wire with a label to record its initial position
from the inboard or the outboard transducer.

F. Transducer Installation
SUBTASK 32-42-11-860-005
(1) Make sure that these circuit breakers are open and have safety tags:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3
Row Col Number Name
E 16 C00196 LANDING GEAR ANTISKID INBD
E 18 C00195 LANDING GEAR ANTISKID OUTBD
SUBTASK 32-42-11-860-002
(2) If the support [11] came out of the axle, install the support in the axle with the slot on the back
of the support at the top.
SUBTASK 32-42-11-420-001
(3) Do these steps to install the transducer [14]:
(a) Before you connect the electrical connector [12] to the back of the transducer [14],
examine the electrical connector [12] for corrosion.
WARNING
DO THE STEPS BELOW IF THE AIRPLANE OPERATES WHERE
DEICING FLUID THAT CONTAINS POTASSIUM FORMATE OR
POTASSIUM ACETATE IS USED. ALSO, DO THE STEPS FOR ALL
AIRPLANES THAT YOU FOUND CORROSION IN THE ELECTRICAL
CONNECTORS IN THE MAIN WHEEL WELL. THE ELECTRICAL
CONNECTORS ARE IN A SYSTEM THAT IS NECESSARY FOR SAFE
FLIGHT.
(b) If there was corrosion, correct the problem (SWPM 20-60-03).
(c) Apply the D5026NS or ZC-026 compound, G50171, to the connector (SWPM 20-60-03).
(d) Wind the electrical wire so that the overall coil diameter is approximately 50% of the
internal diameter of the landing gear axle diameter.
NOTE: If not coiled, the wire bundle section inside the axle is somewhat stiff and may
result in hard contact with the inside of the axle.
(e) Connect the electrical connector [12] to the back of the transducer [14].
NOTE: Use the label on each electrical connector/wire to find the correct position from
the inboard or the outboard transducer.
CAUTION
DO NOT PULL OR TWIST THE WIRE HARNESS WHEN YOU INSTALL
THE TRANSDUCER IN THE AXLE. YOU CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE
WIRES AND THE ANTISKID TRANSDUCER.
(f) Install the transducer [14] in the axle.
1) Install the transducer [14] in the assembly with the tab on the back of the transducer
aligned with the slot inside the support [11].
(g) Do these steps to install the locknut [13]:
1) Install the locknut [13] in its position in the support.
2) Tighten the locknut [13] to 40 ft-lb (54 N·m) - 60 ft-lb (81 N·m) with the locknut
wrench set, SPL-1873.
3) Loosen the locknut [13] to 0 ft-lb (0 N·m).
4) Tighten the locknut [13] to 30 ft-lb (41 N·m).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
5) Install the MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, between the locknut [13] and lockwire
holes in the support [11] (TASK 20-10-44-400-801).
SUBTASK 32-42-11-860-003
(4) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3
Row Col Number Name
E 16 C00196 LANDING GEAR ANTISKID INBD
E 18 C00195 LANDING GEAR ANTISKID OUTBD
SUBTASK 32-42-11-860-004
(5) Do this task: Transducer Operational Test, TASK 32-42-00-710-802.
SUBTASK 32-42-11-420-002
(6) Do these steps to install the bolts [10] to lock the support [11] to the axle assembly:
(a) Install the bolts [10] with the head to the inside of the axle.
(b) Install the washers [9] and nuts [8].
(c) Do a check of the self locking nuts (TASK 20-50-11-910-801).
(d) Tighten the nuts [8] to 63 in-lb (7.1 N·m) - 67 in-lb (7.6 N·m).
SUBTASK 32-42-11-420-003
CAUTION
DO NOT TIGHTEN THE HUBCAP BOLTS TOO MUCH. MAKE SURE THAT THE
HUBCAP IS IN THE CORRECT POSITION BEFORE YOU TIGHTEN THE
BOLTS. TOO MUCH TORQUE WILL CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE BOLTS AND
THE HUBCAP.
(7) Do these steps to install the hubcap [3]:
(a) Turn the transducer drive coupling the inside the wheel assembly [1] such that the drive
on the hubcap [3] and the dog in the wheel will connect when the hubcap [3] is installed.
(b) Put the hubcap [3] in its position on the wheel assembly [1].
1) Turn it if it is necessary to engage the drive on the hubcap [3] with the drive coupling
on the transducer [14].
(c) See the hubcap [3] flush with the wheel assembly [1].
NOTE: Use a soft mallet to lightly tap the hubcap to make it flush.
(d) Install the bolts [6] and washers [7] to attach the hubcap [3] to the wheel assembly [1].
(e) Tighten the bolts [6] to 50 in-lb (6 N·m) - 80 in-lb (9 N·m).
(f) Install MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, on the bolts [6] (TASK 20-10-44-400-801).
(g) Do these steps for the outboard wheel:
1) Put the hubcap fairing [5] on the hubcap [3].
2) Turn the CAM-LOCs [4] fasteners 1/4 turn to attach the hubcap fairing [5] to the
hubcap [3].

D. Antiskid Valve Removal
CAUTION
BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU DISCONNECT THE HYDRAULIC LINES, UNIONS,
FILTERS, AND CHECK VALVES FROM THE ANTISKID VALVES. DAMAGE TO
THE ANTISKID VALVES CAN OCCUR.
SUBTASK 32-42-31-020-001
(1) Disconnect the electrical connector [14] from the antiskid control valve [6].
SUBTASK 32-42-31-020-002
(2) For the UPR normal antiskid control valve [6], do these steps:
(a) Disconnect the pressure hydraulic line [17] and pressure hydraulic line [20] from the
filter [4].
(b) Disconnect the return hydraulic line [16] from the union [12].
(c) Disconnect the brake hydraulic line [15] from the union [12].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135,
138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236;  239-298, 301-304, 306, 308,
315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999 PRE SB 737-32-1528 (Continued)
SUBTASK 32-42-31-020-011
(3) For the LWR normal antiskid control valve [6], do these steps:
(a) Disconnect the pressure hydraulic line [20] from the filter [4].
(b) Disconnect the return hydraulic line [16] and return hydraulic line [21] from the union [12].
(c) Disconnect the brake hydraulic line [22] from the union [12].
SUBTASK 32-42-31-020-005
(4) For the alternate antiskid control valve [6], do these steps:
(a) Disconnect the pressure hydraulic line [25] and pressure hydraulic line [26] from the
filter [4].
(b) Disconnect the return hydraulic line [24] from the check valve [13].
(c) Disconnect the brake hydraulic line [23] from the union [12].
SUBTASK 32-42-31-420-007
(5) Install the caps or plugs on the hydraulic lines.
SUBTASK 32-42-31-020-003
(6) Remove the bolts [8] and washers [7] to remove the antiskid control valve [6] from the airplane.
SUBTASK 32-42-31-020-004
(7) If the normal replacement antiskid control valve [6] does not have hydraulic fittings installed, do
these steps:
(a) Remove the unions [12] and packings [5].
(b) Remove the filter [11] and packing [10].
(c) Remove the filter [4] and packing [5].
(d) Discard the packings [5] and packing [10].
SUBTASK 32-42-31-020-012
(8) If the alternate replacement antiskid control valve [6] does not have hydraulic fittings installed,
do these steps:
(a) Remove the union [12] and packing [5].
(b) Remove the filter [11] and packing [10].
(c) Remove the check valve [13] and packing [5].
(d) Remove the filter [4] and packing [5].
(e) Discard the packings [5] and packing [10].
SUBTASK 32-42-31-480-004
(9) Install plugs in the ports of the antiskid control valve [6].

F. Antiskid Valve Installation
SUBTASK 32-42-31-080-001
(1) Remove the plugs from the ports of the antiskid control valve [6].
SUBTASK 32-42-31-420-001
(2) If the replacement antiskid control valve [6] does not have hydraulic fittings installed, do these
steps:
(a) Lubricate the hydraulic union [12], check valve [13], filter [4], filter [11], packing [10], and
packings [5] for the antiskid control valve [6] with hydraulic fluid, D00153.
(b) Install the new packings [5] on the hydraulic fittings and install the new packing [10] on
the filter [11].
(c) Install the fittings in the antiskid control valve [6].
1) Install the filter [11] in the brake port of the antiskid control valve [6].
a) Tighten the filter [11] to 475 in-lb (53.7 N·m) - 525 in-lb (59.3 N·m).
2) Install the hydraulic union [12] in the brake port of the antiskid control valve [6].
a) Tighten the hydraulic union [12] to 256 in-lb (28.9 N·m) - 284 in-lb (32.1 N·m).
3) Install the fitting in the return port.
a) For the normal antiskid valves, install the hydraulic union [12] in the return port
of the normal antiskid control valve [6].
<1> Tighten the hydraulic union [12] to 161 in-lb (18.2 N·m) - 179 in-lb
(20.2 N·m).

(d) While you hold the ENABLE/VERIFY switch, push and hold the VERIFY switch on the
Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit.
(e) Release the ENABLE/VERIFY switch and the VERIFY switch at the same time.
NOTE: The Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit display will show BRK A/B1 during the test.

(c) While you hold the ENABLE/VERIFY switch, push and hold the VERIFY switch on the
Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit.
(d) Release the ENABLE/VERIFY switch and the VERIFY switch at the same time.
NOTE: The Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit display will show BRK A/B3 during the test.
(e) Make sure the AUTOBRAKE DISARM light on the P2-2 panel comes on.
(f) Set the autobrake selector switch on the P2-2 panel to “OFF”.
SUBTASK 32-42-61-860-017
(12) Do the steps that follow for the autobrake selector position “MAX”.
(a) Set the autobrake selector switch on the P2-2 panel to “MAX”.
(b) Push and hold the ENABLE/VERIFY switch on the Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit.
(c) While you hold the ENABLE/VERIFY switch, push and hold the VERIFY switch on the
Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit.
(d) Release the ENABLE/VERIFY switch and the VERIFY switch at the same time.
NOTE: The Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit display will show BRK A/B4 during the test.
(e) Make sure the AUTOBRAKE DISARM light on the P2-2 panel comes on.
(f) Set the autobrake selector switch on the P2-2 panel to “OFF”.
SUBTASK 32-42-61-860-018
(13) Do the steps that follow for autobrake selector position “RTO”.
(a) Set the autobrake selector switch on the P2-2 panel to “RTO”.
(b) Push and hold the ENABLE/VERIFY switch on the Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit.
(c) While you hold the ENABLE/VERIFY switch, push and hold the VERIFY switch on the
Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit.
(d) Release the ENABLE/VERIFY switch and the VERIFY switch at the same time.
NOTE: The Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit display will show BRK RTO during the test.
(e) Make sure the AUTOBRAKE DISARM light on the P2-2 panel comes on.
(f) Set the autobrake selector switch on the P2-2 panel to “OFF”.
SUBTASK 32-42-61-860-019
(14) Do the steps that follow to test the brake metered pressure switches.
(a) Set the autobrake selector switch on the P2-2 panel to “1”.
(b) Push and hold the left brake pedal to the stop.
(c) Verify that the AUTOBRAKE DISARM light on the P2-2 panel comes on.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(d) Set the autobrake selector switch on the P2-2 panel to “OFF” and then set it back to “1”.
(e) Push and hold the right brake pedal to the stop.
(f) Verify that the AUTOBRAKE DISARM light on the P2-2 panel comes on.
SUBTASK 32-42-61-860-020
(15) Set the autobrake selector switch on the P2-2 panel to “OFF”.
SUBTASK 32-42-61-860-021
(16) Set the BRAKE TEST selector switch on the Antiskid/Autobrake Control Unit to NORM.

E. Autobrake Shuttle Valve Installation
SUBTASK 32-42-71-080-001
(1) Remove the plugs from the ports of the autobrake shuttle valve [3].
SUBTASK 32-42-71-420-001
(2) If the replacement autobrake shuttle valve [3] does not have hydraulic fittings installed, do
these steps:
(a) Lubricate the hydraulic unions [5] and new packings [6] for the autobrake shuttle valve [3]
with hydraulic fluid, D00153.
(b) Install the new packings [6] on the hydraulic unions [5].
(c) Install the unions [5] in the three hydraulic ports in the autobrake shuttle valve [3].
SUBTASK 32-42-71-100-001
(3) Do the steps below to help get a good electrical bond between the autobrake shuttle valve [3]
and valve bracket [8]:
(a) To fully clean the mating surface of the valve bracket [8] and autobrake shuttle valve [3],
do this task: Hand Clean Metal Surfaces with Abrasives, TASK 20-10-34-120-801.
(b) Manually apply coating, C00064, to all of the cleaned areas of the valve bracket [8].
(c) Fay surface seal the autobrake shuttle valve [3] to the valve bracket [8] with sealant,
A00247.
SUBTASK 32-42-71-420-003
WARNING
USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COR-BAN
27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH WATER. IF
THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH YOUR EYES
WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL CONTAINS FLAMMABLE
AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL.

(alternate), to the bolts [11] and washers [10] that hold the autobrake shuttle valve [3] to the

 ALL

EQUIPMENT.

Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801.
SUBTASK 32-42-81-480-002
(2) Make sure that the tires have chocks installed around them, do one of these tasks:

TASK 10-11-05-500-801
• Chock Installation in Winds More than 35 Knots - Handling, TASK 10-11-05-500-802.

 ALL
SUBTASK 32-42-81-860-011

this task: Hydraulic Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or Hydraulic
Reservoirs Depressurization, TASK 29-09-00-860-808.
(a) Make sure that the air charging valve stays open until the reservoir air pressure gauge
shows 0 psi (0 kPa).
NOTE: This step makes sure that the reservoirs fully release pressure.

SUBTASK 32-42-81-840-003
(5) Operate the brake pedals until the gage at the brake accumulator shows no change in the
pressure.

approximately 14 times to completely release the pressure from the accumulator. This
will prevent high-pressure fluid spray when replacing components within the hydraulic
brake system.

until the reservoir air pressure gauge shows 0 psi (0 kPa) (TASK 29-09-00-860-802 or
TASK 29-09-00-860-808).
