F. Autobrake Pressure Control Module Installation
SUBTASK 32-42-81-080-001
(1) Remove the caps/plugs, STD-14686, from the ports of the autobrake pressure control
module [20].
SUBTASK 32-42-81-420-001
(2) If the replacement autobrake pressure control module [20] does not have hydraulic fittings
installed, do these steps:
(a) Lubricate the unions [13], union [18], and packings [14] for the autobrake pressure control
module [20] with hydraulic fluid, D00153.
(b) Install the packings [14] on the unions [13] and union [18].
(c) Install the unions [13] and union [18] in the autobrake pressure control module [20].
1) Tighten the unions [13] and union [18] to 360 ±18 in-lb (40.7 ±2.0 N·m).
SUBTASK 32-42-81-100-001
(3) To help get a good electrical bond between the autobrake pressure control module [20] and
module bracket, do these steps:
(a) To fully clean the mating surface of the bracket and autobrake pressure control
module [20], do this task: Hand Clean Metal Surfaces with Abrasives,
TASK 20-10-34-120-801.
(b) Manually apply coating, C00064, to all of the cleaned areas of the bracket.
 ALL; AIRPLANES WITH PARKER HANNIFIN CORP AUTOBRAKE CONTROL MODULE P/N
78169, -01, -02, -03, -04
(c) Fay surface seal the valve assembly to the bracket with sealant, A02315.
 ALL
SUBTASK 32-42-81-420-002
(4) Install the autobrake pressure control module [20].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
WARNING
USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COR￾BAN 27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH
WATER. IF THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH
YOUR EYES WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL
CONTAINS FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO
PERSONNEL.
(a) Apply Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237 (preferred), or corrosion inhibiting material,
G50136 (alternate), to the bolts [3] and washers [4] that hold the autobrake pressure
control module [20] to the bracket.
(b) Install the bolts [3] and washers [4] to hold the autobrake pressure control module [20] to
the bracket.
(c) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the autobrake pressure control
module [20] and bracket (SWPM 20-20-00).
1) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550.
2) Make sure that the resistance is not more than 0.0025 ohms (2.5 milliohms).
(d) Remove the caps/plugs, STD-14686, from the hydraulic line (brake port) [2], hydraulic
line (return port) [9], and hydraulic line (pressure port) [11].
(e) Connect the hydraulic lines to the unions [13] and union [18] on the autobrake pressure
control module [20].
1) Tighten the B-nuts on the hydraulic line (brake port) [2], hydraulic line (return
port) [9], and hydraulic line (pressure port) [11] to 170 ±9 in-lb (19.2 ±1.0 N·m).
(f) Examine the electrical connector [1], electrical connector [6], electrical connector [7], and
electrical connector [8] for corrosion.
WARNING
DO THE STEPS BELOW IF THE AIRPLANE OPERATES WHERE
DEICING FLUID THAT CONTAINS POTASSIUM FORMATE OR
POTASSIUM ACETATE IS USED. ALSO, DO THE STEPS FOR ALL
AIRPLANES THAT YOU FOUND CORROSION IN THE ELECTRICAL
CONNECTORS IN THE MAIN WHEEL WELL. THE ELECTRICAL
CONNECTORS ARE IN A SYSTEM THAT IS NECESSARY FOR SAFE
FLIGHT.
1) If there is corrosion, correct the problem (SWPM 20-60-03).
2) Apply D5026NS or ZC-026 compound, G50171, to the electrical connector [1],
electrical connector [6], electrical connector [7], and electrical connector [8] (SWPM
20-60-03).
(g) Connect the electrical connector [1], electrical connector [6], electrical connector [7], and
electrical connector [8] to the autobrake pressure control module [20].
SUBTASK 32-42-81-390-001
(5) Apply a fillet seal with sealant, A02315, around the mounting points between the autobrake
pressure control module [20] and bracket (SWPM 20-20-00, Section 14E).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

F. Solenoid Valve Removal
SUBTASK 32-42-81-020-005
(1) Remove the screws [25] and washers [26] that connect the solenoid valve assembly [12] to the
autobrake pressure control module [20].
SUBTASK 32-42-81-480-007
CAUTION
WHEN YOU REMOVE THE SOLENOID VALVE FROM THE MODULE, MAKE
SURE THE VALVE IS KEPT IN A VERTICAL POSITION. IF THE VALVE IS NOT
KEPT IN A VERTICAL POSITION, DAMAGE TO THE CONNECTOR PINS CAN
OCCUR.
CAUTION
WHEN YOU REMOVE THE SOLENOID VALVE AND THE GASKET, MAKE
SURE THAT CONTAMINATION CAN NOT GO INTO THE MODULE'S OPEN
PORTS. DAMAGE TO THE VALVE CAN OCCUR IF LET CONTAMINATION GO
INTO THE PORTS.
(2) Remove the solenoid valve assembly [12] from the autobrake pressure control module [20].
SUBTASK 32-42-81-480-008
(3) Remove the packing [24] from the solenoid valve assembly [12].
(a) Discard the packing [24].
SUBTASK 32-42-81-020-006
(4) Remove the gasket [27] from the autobrake pressure control module [20].
SUBTASK 32-42-81-480-009
(5) Install the cap/plug, STD-14686, in the port of the solenoid valve assembly [12].
G. Servo Valve Removal
SUBTASK 32-42-81-020-007
(1) Disconnect the electrical connector [7] from the servo valve assembly [10].
SUBTASK 32-42-81-020-008
(2) Remove the screws [22] and washers [23] (if applicable) that connect the servo valve
assembly [10] to the autobrake pressure control module [20].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 32-42-81-480-010
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT CONTAMINATION CAN NOT GO INTO THE MODULE'S
OPEN PORTS WHEN YOU REMOVE THE SERVO VALVE AND GASKET.
DAMAGE TO THE VALVE CAN OCCUR IF YOU LET CONTAMINATION GO
INTO THE PORTS.
(3) Remove the servo valve assembly [10] from the autobrake pressure control module [20].
SUBTASK 32-42-81-020-009
(4) Remove the gasket [21].
SUBTASK 32-42-81-480-011
(5) Install the caps/plugs, STD-14686, in the ports of the servo valve assembly [10].

SUBTASK 32-42-81-480-013

switch [5].
(a) Discard the packing [16] and packing [17] (if applicable).
SUBTASK 32-42-81-480-014
(4) Install the cap/plug, STD-14686, in the port of the pressure switch [5].

G. Solenoid Valve Installation
SUBTASK 32-42-81-420-006
(1) Install the packing [24] on the solenoid valve assembly [12].
SUBTASK 32-42-81-480-018
(2) Remove the cap/plug, STD-14686, from the port of the solenoid valve assembly [12].
SUBTASK 32-42-81-480-019
WARNING
USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COR-BAN
27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH WATER. IF
THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH YOUR EYES
WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL CONTAINS FLAMMABLE
AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL.
(3) Apply Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237, (preferred) or corrosion inhibiting material, G50136,
(optional) to the screws [25].
SUBTASK 32-42-81-020-012
(4) Install the solenoid valve gasket [27] on the autobrake pressure control module [20].
SUBTASK 32-42-81-020-013
(5) Put the solenoid valve assembly [12] in its position on the autobrake pressure control
module [20].
SUBTASK 32-42-81-420-007
(6) Install the screws [25] and washers [26] to connect the solenoid valve assembly [12] to the
autobrake pressure control module [20].
(a) Tighten the screws [25] to 75 in-lb (8.47 N·m) - 80 in-lb (9.04 N·m) in a crisscross
sequence.
1) Starting with the screw [25] closest to the nearest mounting bolt [3] for the
autobrake pressure control module [20], tighten all bolts to 5 in-lb (0.56 N·m) -
10 in-lb (1.13 N·m), then to 35 in-lb (3.95 N·m) - 40 in-lb (4.52 N·m), and then to the
final torque.
SUBTASK 32-42-81-420-009
(7) Use a 0.0015 in. (0.0381 mm) shim stock to examine the gasket [27] for gaps.
(a) No gaps more than 0.0015 in. (0.0381 mm) are permitted.
NOTE: This applies to gaps on either side of the gasket. There must be no gap in excess
of 0.0015 in. (0.0381 mm) between the solenoid valve and the gasket and
between the valve module and the gasket.
H. Servo Valve Installation
SUBTASK 32-42-81-480-020
(1) Remove the caps/plugs, STD-14686, from the ports of the servo valve assembly [10].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 32-42-81-480-021
WARNING
USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COR-BAN
27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH WATER. IF
THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH YOUR EYES
WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL CONTAINS FLAMMABLE
AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL.
(2) Apply Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237, (preferred) or corrosion inhibiting material, G50136,
(optional) to the screws [22].
SUBTASK 32-42-81-020-014
(3) Install the servo valve gasket [21] on the autobrake pressure control module [20].
SUBTASK 32-42-81-020-015
(4) Put the servo valve assembly [10] in its position on the autobrake pressure control
module [20].
SUBTASK 32-42-81-420-010
(5) Install the screws [22] and washers [23] (if applicable) to connect the servo valve
assembly [10] to the autobrake pressure control module [20].
(a) Tighten the screws [22] to 75 in-lb (8.47 N·m) - 80 in-lb (9.04 N·m) in a crisscross
sequence.
1) Starting with the screw [22] closest to the solenoid valve assembly [12], tighten all
screws [22] to 5 in-lb (0.56 N·m) - 10 in-lb (1.13 N·m), then to 35 in-lb (3.95 N·m) -
40 in-lb (4.52 N·m), and then to the final torque.
SUBTASK 32-42-81-420-012
(6) Use a 0.0015 in. (0.0381 mm) shim stock to examine the gasket [21] for gaps.
(a) No gaps more than 0.0015 in. (0.0381 mm) are permitted.
NOTE: This applies to gaps on either side of the gasket. There must be no gap in excess
of 0.0015 in. (0.0381 mm) between the servo valve and the gasket and between
the valve module and the gasket.
SUBTASK 32-42-81-020-016
(7) Examine the electrical connector [7] for corrosion.
WARNING
DO THE STEPS BELOW IF THE AIRPLANE OPERATES WHERE
DEICING FLUID THAT CONTAINS POTASSIUM FORMATE OR
POTASSIUM ACETATE IS USED. ALSO, DO THE STEPS FOR ALL
AIRPLANES THAT YOU FOUND CORROSION IN THE ELECTRICAL
CONNECTORS IN THE MAIN WHEEL WELL. THE ELECTRICAL
CONNECTORS ARE IN A SYSTEM THAT IS NECESSARY FOR SAFE
FLIGHT.
(a) If there was corrosion, refer to SWPM 20-60-03 to correct the problem.
(b) Apply theD5026NS or ZC-026 compound, G50171, to the connector (SWPM 20-60-03).
SUBTASK 32-42-81-420-023
(8) Connect the electrical connector [7] to the servo valve assembly [10].

 ALL

SUBTASK 32-42-81-480-024
(4) Remove the cap/plug, STD-14686, from the port of the pressure switch [5].
SUBTASK 32-42-81-480-022
(5) Install the pressure switch [5] on the autobrake pressure control module [20].
(a) Make sure that you verify the type of pressure switch installed on the control module.
NOTE: Pressure switch units are interchangeable.
(b) For Parker Hannifin Corp (P/N 78169 series) pressure switch, tighten the pressure
switch [5] to 90 in-lb (10.2 N·m) - 110 in-lb (12.4 N·m).
(c) For Woodward HRT (P/N 20102060 series) pressure switch, tighten the pressure
switch [5] to 342 in-lb (38.64 N·m) - 378 in-lb (42.71 N·m).
(d) For Custom Control Sensors, Inc (P/N 90G237 series) pressure switch, tighten the
pressure switch [5] to 145 in-lb (16.4 N·m) - 155 in-lb (17.5 N·m).
SUBTASK 32-42-81-420-017
(6) Examine the electrical connector [1] or electrical connector [6] for corrosion.

DEICING FLUID THAT CONTAINS POTASSIUM FORMATE OR

(a) If there was corrosion, refer to SWPM 20-60-03 to correct the problem.

electrical connector [6] (SWPM 20-60-03).

F. Parking Brake System - Adjustment
SUBTASK 32-44-00-820-005
(1) Adjust the pawls [11] of the parking brake (Figure 501):
(a) Push the two brake pedals fully to the pedal steps, and hold them in position.
(b) Extend the pawls [11] one turn at a time until the parking brake can not be set.
(c) Retract the pawls [11] 1 to 2 turns to set adjustment or until you get a clearance of
0.04 in. (1.0 mm) - 0.10 in. (2.5 mm) between the pawl [11] and bushing [12].
(d) Make sure that the parking brake can be set from the captain's and first officer's seat.
(e) If necessary, adjust the pawls [11] (retract one turn at a time) until the parking brake can
be set from the captain's or first officer's seat.
NOTE: The more the pawls are retracted, the larger the parking brake bleed-down rate
will be.
(f) Lock the adjustment.
(g) Release the brake pedals.
SUBTASK 32-44-00-820-002
(2) Adjust the pawl stop (Figure 501):
(a) Turn the bellcranks [13] until the bushings [12] are at their closest point to the aft edge of
the pawls [11].
(b) Adjust the pawl stop until the clearance between the aft edge of the pawls [11] and the
bushings [12] is 0.16 in. (4.1 mm) – 0.20 in. (5.1 mm):
1) Remove the nut [7] from the pawl stop assembly.
2) Remove the bumper [4], screw [5], and washer [6] from the pawl stop bracket [8].
3) Add or remove washers [6] until you get the correct clearance.
4) Install the bumper [4], screw [5], and washer [6] on the pawl stop bracket [8].
5) Install the nut [7] on the pawl stop assembly.
(c) Release the bellcrank [13].
SUBTASK 32-44-00-820-003
(3) Adjust the parking brake lever [42] (Figure 501, Figure 502):
(a) Install a rig pin LGB2, from rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, through the jackshaft rig pin
hole [15] and switch support bracket [18].
(b) Install rig pin LGB1, from rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, through the brake control bell cranks
rig pin hole [3] rig pin hole and the left beam structure rig pin hole [49].
(c) Remove the cotter pin [47], washer [46], and the pin [45] from the parking brake lever [42]
and the rod [44].
(d) Loosen the jamnut [48] on the bottom of the rod [44].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(e) Adjust the length of the rod [44] until the stop surface of the parking brake lever [42] is
against the top of the control stand when the pin [45] is installed.
NOTE: If the parking brake rod is adjusted with this method, the rod itself must be turned
in full 360 degree turns. The rod assembly is orientation sensitive.
(f) Tighten the jamnut [48] on the rod [44].
(g) Install the pin [45], washer [46], and the cotter pin [47] to hold the parking brake lever [42]
to the rod [44].
(h) Make sure that the parking brake lever [42] moves smoothly.
(i) Remove the rig pin from rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, the jackshaft rig pin hole [15] and the
switch support bracket [18].
(j) Remove the rig pin LGB1 from rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, the left beam structure rig pin
hole [49] and the hole on the brake control bell cranks rig pin hole [3] rig pin hole.
SUBTASK 32-44-00-820-004
(4) Adjust the parking brake latch switch [17] (Figure 501, Figure 502):
(a) Make sure that the rudder pedals are released.
(b) Pull the parking brake lever [42] on the control stand, until it stops, and hold it in this
position.
(c) Make sure that the switch actuator [16] lightly contacts the rod end.
(d) Make sure that the parking brake light [43], next to the parking brake lever [42], does not
turn on.
(e) If the switch [17] does not operate in the correct range, do these steps:
1) Install the rig pin LGB1, from rigging pin kit, SPL-1585, to the brake control bell
cranks rig pin hole [3] on captain side and left beam structure rig pin hole [49].
2) Loosen the screws [19] or nuts [20] that hold the switch actuator [16] and switch [17]
to the structure.
3) Rotate the pawls [11] until they touch the bellcrank bushing [12].
4) Adjust the switch actuator [16] until the switch actuator roller [21] touches the end of
the rod [1].
5) Continue to rotate switch [17] until the switch clicks.
6) Back of the switch slightly until the switch clicks
7) Tighten the screws [19] or nuts [20] to 2 in-lb (0.2 N·m) - 3 in-lb (0.3 N·m) above the
run-on torque value.
8) Remove the rig pin LGB1, from rigging pin kit, SPL-1585.
(f) Push the two rudder pedals and set the parking brake.
(g) Make sure that the parking brake light [43] next to the parking brake lever [42] turns on.
NOTE: The parking brake light should turn on between 35 and 45 degrees of parking
brake lever travel from the released position.
(h) Release the parking brake.
(i) Make sure that parking brake light [43] goes off.
(j) Make sure that the parking brake lever [42] returns to its usual position without
assistance.
(k) Set the parking brake.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 32-44-00-860-004
(5) Close this access panel:

112A Forward Access Door

SUBTASK 32-44-00-480-003
(1) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811.
SUBTASK 32-44-00-480-004
WARNING
MAKE SURE THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE LANDING
GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR COULD
RETRACT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(2) If the downlock pins are not installed in the nose and main landing gear, do this task: Landing
Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801.
SUBTASK 32-44-00-860-005
(3) For the system A and system B hydraulic systems, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B
Power Removal, TASK 29-11-00-860-805.
SUBTASK 32-44-00-480-005
(4) Make sure the tires have chocks installed around them (CHOCK INSTALLATION,
PAGEBLOCK 10-11-05/201).
SUBTASK 32-44-00-860-006
(5) Release the parking brake.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 32-44-00-840-001
(6) Fully push the brake pedals 12 times to remove hydraulic pressure from the brake
accumulator.
NOTE: You can look at the brake pistons to see that the brakes no longer actuate when the
brake pedals are pushed.
SUBTASK 32-44-00-480-006
(7) Install rig pins R1 and R2 through the captain's and first officer's rudder pedal shaft rig pin
holes [2] and into the structure. The rigging pins are from rigging pin kit, SPL-1585.
NOTE: The placard on the inside of the box for the rigging pin kit identifies the different rigging
pins.
E. Procedure
SUBTASK 32-44-00-790-001
WARNING
KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL
SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE
COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC
POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(1) For the B hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization,
TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
SUBTASK 32-44-00-720-001
(2) Make sure that the pressure shown on the HYD BRAKE PRESS gage is approximately the
same as the B hydraulic system pressure.
NOTE: The HYD BRAKE PRESS gage is in the flight compartment on the main instrument
panel for the first officer.
SUBTASK 32-44-00-710-001
(3) Do these steps for the captain's brake pedals:
(a) Push the two brake pedals fully to their stops and set the parking brake.
(b) Release the brake pedals.
(c) Make sure the parking brake engages.
(d) Make sure the parking brake light on the control stand is on.
(e) Look at the pistons on each brake to see that the brakes are engaged.
(f) Release the parking brake.
(g) Make sure the parking brake light on the control stand is off.
(h) Look at the pistons on each brake to see that the brakes are not engaged.
(i) For the B hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal,
TASK 29-11-00-860-805
(j) Fully push the captain's brake pedals twelve times to remove the pressure from the brake
accumulator.
(k) Push the two brake pedals fully to their stops and set the parking brake.
(l) Release the brake pedals.
(m) Make sure the parking brake engages.
(n) Make sure the parking brake light on the control stand is on.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(o) Look at the pistons on each brake to see that the brakes are not engaged.
(p) Release the parking brake.
WARNING
KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL
SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR.
THESE COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY
HYDRAULIC POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(q) For the B hydraulic system, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization,
TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
(r) Push the left brake pedal fully to the stop.
(s) Pull the parking brake lever on the control stand.
(t) Make sure the parking brake will not engage.
(u) Make sure the parking brake light on the control stand is off.
(v) Look at the pistons on each brake to see that the brakes on the left gear are engaged
and the brakes on the right gear are not engaged.
(w) Release the left brake pedal.
(x) Push the right brake pedal fully to the stop.
(y) Pull the parking brake lever on the control stand.
(z) Make sure the parking brake will not engage.
(aa) Make sure the parking brake light on the control stand is off.
(ab) Look at the pistons on each brake to see that the brakes on the right gear are engaged
and the brakes on the left gear are not engaged.
(ac) Release the right brake pedal.
SUBTASK 32-44-00-710-002
(4) Do these steps for the first officer's brake pedals:
(a) Push the two brake pedals fully to their stops and set the parking brake.
(b) Release the brake pedals.
(c) Make sure the parking brake engages.
(d) Release the parking brake.
(e) Push the left brake pedal fully to the stop.
(f) Pull the parking brake lever on the control stand.
(g) Make sure the parking brake will not engage.
(h) Release the left brake pedal.
(i) Push the right brake pedal fully to the stop.
(j) Pull the parking brake lever on the control stand.
(k) Make sure the parking brake will not engage.
(l) Release the right brake pedal.
SUBTASK 32-44-00-080-001
(5) Remove rig pins R1 and R2 from the rudder pedal shaft [2].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 32-44-00-720-002
(6) Do this task: Parking Brake Hold Check, TASK 32-44-00-790-801.
32-44-00-790-801Parking Brake Hold CheckPDF p. 1754
4. Parking Brake Hold Check
NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. General
(1) This task includes these steps:
(a) Parking brake system bleed down test - parking brake set
(b) Parking brake system bleed down test - parking brake released.
B. References
Reference Title
10-11-05 P/B 201 CHOCK INSTALLATION
29-11-00-860-801 Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization (P/B 201)
29-11-00-860-805 Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal (P/B 201)

C. Location Zones
Zone Area
211 Flight Compartment - Left
734 Left Main Landing Gear
744 Right Main Landing Gear
D. Prepare for the Check
SUBTASK 32-44-00-480-007
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE
LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR
CAN RETRACT. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS, AND DAMAGE
TO EQUIPMENT.
(1) If the downlock pins are not installed in the nose and main landing gear, do this task: Landing
Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801.
SUBTASK 32-44-00-480-008
(2) Make sure the tires have chocks installed around them (PAGEBLOCK 10-11-05/201).
SUBTASK 32-44-00-860-007
(3) Release the parking brake.
SUBTASK 32-44-00-860-008
(4) For the A and B hydraulic systems, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal,
TASK 29-11-00-860-805.
SUBTASK 32-44-00-870-001
(5) Push the Captain's or the First Officer's left and right toe brake pedals to the stops several
times until the brakes no longer actuate.
NOTE: This will release the hydraulic pressure at the accumulator.
(a) Check the pistons on each brake to make sure that the brakes no longer actuate when
the brake pedals are pushed.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 32-44-00-860-009
(6) Make sure that the brake accumulator Nitrogen charge is correct.
NOTE: Correct charge pressure from the accumulator placard are located on the rear
bulkhead in the right main gear wheel well.
SUBTASK 32-44-00-790-002
WARNING
KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL
SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE
COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC
POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(7) To pressurize B hydraulic system to 3000 ±150 psig (20,684 ±1034 kPa), do this task:
Hydraulic System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
SUBTASK 32-44-00-860-010
(8) Set the parking brake.
NOTE: This step keeps the brake system pressurized with the accumulator.
SUBTASK 32-44-00-720-003
(9) Wait at least 10 minutes for the accumulator temperature to stabilize.
E. Parking Brake Hold Check - Parking Brake Set
SUBTASK 32-44-00-720-004
(1) Write down the pressure shown on the PRESS gage for the brake accumulator.
NOTE: The PRESS gage is located on the rear bulkhead in the right main gear wheel well.
SUBTASK 32-44-00-860-011
(2) For the B hydraulic systems, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal,
TASK 29-11-00-860-805.
NOTE: This will leave the accumulator charged and pressurized.
(a) Record the initial time when the B hydraulic system pressure is removed.
SUBTASK 32-44-00-710-003
(3) Do a check of the brake pressure at the end of any of the time periods that follow. If the
necessary pressure drop for one time period is not within the limits, use the next time period.
NOTE: It is permitted to read the brake pressure from the brake pressure gage in the cockpit,
or the brake accumulator gage in the wheel well.
(a) After 10 minutes, the pressure drop should be less than 100 psi (689 kPa).
(b) After 30 minutes, the pressure drop should be less than 300 psi (2068 kPa).
(c) After 1 hour, the pressure drop should be less than 500 psi (3447 kPa).
(d) After 8 hours, the pressure should be greater than 1200 psi (8274 kPa) minimum.
SUBTASK 32-44-00-780-001
(4) If the brake accumulator pressure drops faster than permitted, do a check for leaks in the
accumulator system.
SUBTASK 32-44-00-780-002
(5) The trouble shooting of the brake system can be delayed until the next convenient
maintenance period if the conditions that follow are met:
(a) With the parking brake set, make sure that the brake accumulator pressure drop is less
than 800 psi (5516 kPa) in the first 30 minutes.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) The system passes the parking brake hold check - parking brake released.
SUBTASK 32-44-00-860-012
(6) Release the parking brake.
SUBTASK 32-44-00-720-005
(7) Push the Captain's or First Officer's left and right toe brake pedals to the stops 7 times while
observing the brake pistons on all of the brakes.
NOTE: Wait approximately 3 seconds each time you apply the brakes.
(a) Make sure that the brake pistons compress and release each of the 7 times the pedals
are pushed.
F. Parking Brake Hold Check - Parking Brake Released
SUBTASK 32-44-00-790-003
WARNING
KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL
SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE
COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC
POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(1) Pressurize B hydraulic system to 3000 ±150 psig (20,684 ±1034 kPa), do this task: Hydraulic
System A or B Pressurization, TASK 29-11-00-860-801.
SUBTASK 32-44-00-720-006
(2) Wait at least 10 minutes for the accumulator temperature to stabilize.
SUBTASK 32-44-00-720-007
(3) Write down the pressure shown on the PRESS gage for the brake accumulator.
NOTE: The PRESS gage is located on the rear bulkhead in the right main gear wheel well.
SUBTASK 32-44-00-860-013
(4) For the B hydraulic systems, do this task: Hydraulic System A or B Power Removal,
TASK 29-11-00-860-805.
NOTE: This will leave the accumulator charged and pressurized.
(a) Record the initial time when the B hydraulic system pressure is removed.
SUBTASK 32-44-00-780-003
(5) Do a check of the brake pressure at 30 minutes after the test start.
(a) Make sure that the pressure decrease of the brake accumulator is less than 450 psi
(3103 kPa).
SUBTASK 32-44-00-780-004
(6) If the brake accumulator pressure drops faster than permitted, do a check the accumulator
system for leaks.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
G. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 32-44-00-790-004
WARNING
KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL

SUBTASK 32-44-00-720-009
(2) Set the parking brake.
SUBTASK 32-44-00-860-014

TASK 29-11-00-860-805.

F. Parking Brake Shutoff Valve Installation
SUBTASK 32-44-21-080-001
(1) Remove the plugs or caps from the ports of the parking brake shutoff valve assy [5].
SUBTASK 32-44-21-420-001
(2) If the replacement parking brake shutoff valve assy [5] does not have hydraulic fittings
installed, do these steps:
(a) Lubricate the reducer [3], reducer [7] and packings [4] for the parking brake shutoff valve
assy [5] with hydraulic fluid, D00153, or MCS 352B fluid, D00054.
(b) Install the packing [4] on the reducer [3].
(c) Install the reducer [3] in the parking brake shutoff valve assy [5].
(d) Install the packing [4] on the reducer [7].
(e) Install the reducer [7] in the parking brake shutoff valve assy [5].
SUBTASK 32-44-21-100-001
(3) Do the steps below to help get a good electrical bond between the valve assy [5] and the
support bracket:
(a) To fully clean the mating surface of the support bracket and the valve assy [5], do this
task: Hand Clean Metal Surfaces with Abrasives, TASK 20-10-34-120-801.
(b) For all cleaned areas, and if there is any damage to the finish on the valve assy [5],
manually apply coating, C00064.
SUBTASK 32-44-21-390-001
WARNING
USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION WHEN YOU USE COR-BAN
27L. IF IT GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH WATER. IF
THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH YOUR EYES
WITH WATER. GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL CONTAINS FLAMMABLE
AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL.
(4) Apply a layer of the Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237, (preferred) or corrosion inhibiting
material, G50136, (alternate), to the threads and the shank of each bolt [2].
(a) Do not let the Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237, or corrosion inhibiting material, G50136,
dry before you install the bolts [2].
(b) Install the bolts [2] when the Cor-Ban 27L Compound, G50237, or corrosion inhibiting
material, G50136, is wet.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 32-44-21-390-003
WARNING
USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION AGAINST CORROSION
INHIBITOR MATERIAL, G50136. IF CORROSION INHIBITOR MATERIAL,
G50136 GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH WATER. IF
THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH YOUR EYES
WITH WATER AND GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL CONTAINS VERY
POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO
PERSONNEL.
(5) Apply a layer of corrosion inhibiting material, G50136, to the mating surface of the mounting
bracket.
NOTE: Do not let corrosion inhibiting material, G50136, dry before the bolts installation.
SUBTASK 32-44-21-420-002
(6) Hold the parking brake shutoff valve assy [5] in its position on the airplane.
SUBTASK 32-44-21-420-003
(7) Install the bolt [2] and washer [1] which hold the parking brake shutoff valve assy [5] to the
airplane.
SUBTASK 32-44-21-210-001
(8) Make sure that there is squeeze-out around mating surfaces of the support bracket and
parking brake shutoff valve assy [5].
SUBTASK 32-44-21-100-002
WARNING
USE NITRILE GLOVES FOR SKIN PROTECTION AGAINST CORROSION
INHIBITOR MATERIAL, G50136. IF CORROSION INHIBITOR MATERIAL,
G50136 GETS ON YOUR SKIN, IMMEDIATELY REMOVE IT WITH WATER. IF
THIS MATERIAL GETS IN YOUR EYES, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH YOUR EYES
WITH WATER AND GET MEDICAL AID. THIS MATERIAL CONTAINS VERY
POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE AGENTS WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO
PERSONNEL.
(9) If it is necessary, remove the excess of corrosion inhibiting material, G50136, with a dry
lint-free cloth, G01043.
NOTE: The stains of the corrosion inhibiting material, G50136, remaining in crevices are
acceptable.
SUBTASK 32-44-21-760-001
(10) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550, to measure the electrical
resistance between the valve assy [5] and the bracket.
(a) Make sure that the resistance is less than 0.0025 ohms.
(b) If the measured resistance is not less than 0.0025 ohms, do the steps to clean the mating
surfaces of the bracket and valve assy [5].
(c) Apply coating, C00064, again.
SUBTASK 32-44-21-080-002
(11) Remove the caps or plugs from the elbow and the tee fitting.
SUBTASK 32-44-21-420-004
(12) Connect the tee fitting to the reducer [3] on the parking brake shutoff valve assy [5].
SUBTASK 32-44-21-420-005
(13) Connect the elbow to the reducer [7] on the parking brake shutoff valve assy [5].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 32-44-21-420-006
(14) Before you connect the electrical connector [6] to the parking brake shutoff valve assy [5],
examine the connector for corrosion.
WARNING
DO THE STEPS BELOW IF THE AIRPLANE OPERATES WHERE
DEICING FLUID THAT CONTAINS POTASSIUM FORMATE OR
POTASSIUM ACETATE IS USED. ALSO, DO THE STEPS FOR ALL
AIRPLANES THAT YOU FOUND CORROSION IN THE ELECTRICAL
CONNECTORS IN THE MAIN WHEEL WELL. THE ELECTRICAL
CONNECTORS ARE IN A SYSTEM THAT IS NECESSARY FOR SAFE
FLIGHT.
(a) If there was corrosion, correct the problem SWPM 20-60-03.
(b) Apply the D5026NS or ZC-026 compound, G50171, to the connector (SWPM 20-60-03).
(15) Connect the electrical connector [6] to the parking brake shutoff valve assy [5].

 ALL

SURE THAT THEY ARE SAFE. AIR PRESSURE CAN CAUSE AN EXPLOSION
OF THE DAMAGED WHEEL AND TIRE COMPONENTS. INJURIES TO
PERSONNEL, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT ALL PERSONNEL ARE CLEAR OF THE INFLATION VALVE
ASSEMBLY PATH WHILE YOU REMOVE IT. IF THE INFLATION VALVE
ASSEMBLY EJECTS WHILE YOU REMOVE IT, INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN
OCCUR.
(4) Deflate the tire with the small bore tire deflator, COM-4046 or large bore tire deflator,
COM-1524.
NOTE: Always go near the wheels from the front or rear.
NOTE: If the tire is hot, let the tire cool before you deflate it.
WARNING
DO NOT LOOSEN OR REMOVE THE VALVE BODY UNDER PRESSURE.
THE VALVE CAN BLOW OUT CAUSING INJURY TO PERSONNEL.
(a) If you cannot use the usual procedure to deflate the tire because the valve core is
damaged, do these steps:
1) Turn the valve assembly slowly in a counterclockwise direction until there is gas
leakage through the boss.
2) At the same time, push lightly on the valve assembly.
3) After all of the gas has been released, remove the valve assembly from the tire.
E. Inflate the Tire
SUBTASK 32-45-00-600-001
WARNING
USE A PRESSURE SOURCE WITH A REGULATOR TO INFLATE THE TIRES. A
PRESSURE SOURCE WITHOUT A REGULATOR CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO
PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(1) Do this task: Add Nitrogen or Air to the Tire, TASK 12-15-51-610-802.

D. Tires Inspection
SUBTASK 32-45-00-480-004
WARNING
MAKE SURE THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE LANDING
GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR CAN
RETRACT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(1) If the downlock pins are not installed in the nose and main landing gear, do this task: Landing
Gear Downlock Pins Installation, TASK 32-00-01-480-801.
SUBTASK 32-45-00-220-002
(2) Do this task: Landing Gear Tire Pressure Check and Tire Servicing, TASK 12-15-51-780-801.
SUBTASK 32-45-00-210-009
(3) Do the steps that follow and examine the tires (Figure 601, Figure 602):
(a) Examine the tires for air leaks, abrasions, unusual worn areas, cuts, and flat spots.
(b) Examine the tires for the presence of contaminants.
1) Keep the tires clean of contaminants such as oils, fuels, hydraulic fluids, aircraft
cleaning agents, and greases.
2) Cover the tire if these or other potentially harmful chemicals spill on the tire.
3) Wipe off the tire with a soapy solution if the tire becomes contaminated.
4) The tire should be removed from service as soon as practical if the surface of the
tire appears soft, spongy, or there are bulges present.
(c) Remove the tires that have the conditions that follow:
1) Cuts or weather cracks in the grooves, the tread, shoulders or sidewalls that exceed
the limits in (Figure 602).
2) Blisters, bulges, or other signs of ply separation in the tread, shoulder or sidewall
area.
3) Tires with a flat spot which shows the tread reinforcement ply (bias) or cut protector
(radial).
NOTE: If the tread reinforcement ply (bias) or the cut protector (radial) shows, the
tire should be replaced as soon as possible. If necessary, the tire may be
used for a small number of landings until it is replaced. However, you may
not be able to retread the tire if you leave the tire in service too long with
this condition.
4) Other types of damage which can cause tire problems.
(d) Examine the tires for worn areas:
1) Measure the depth of the tire tread groove at three points that are equally apart.
2) If the average depth of any groove is 1/32 inch (0.79 mm) or less, the tire must be
replaced at the next convenient maintenance opportunity.
3) If the tread belt ply (radial) or carcass ply (bias) shows at any location, the tire is not
serviceable and must be replaced.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
4) If the tread is worn so that the cut protector (radial) or tread reinforcement ply (bias)
shows at any location, the tire must be replaced at the next convenient maintenance
opportunity.
NOTE: If the cut protector (radial) or tread reinforcement ply (bias) shows, the tire
should be replaced as soon as possible. If necessary, the tire may be used
for a small number of landings until it is replaced. However, you may not be
able to retread the tire if you leave the tire in service too long with this
condition.

F. Wheel Bearings Inspection
SUBTASK 32-45-00-020-003
(1) Remove the bearing cone from the bearing cup (Figure 603).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 32-45-00-210-014
(2) Put the bearing cone in a clean area.
(a) Make sure that no unwanted materials get into the bearing cone while setting it aside.
SUBTASK 32-45-00-210-011
(3) Examine the internal and external surfaces of the bearing cup and cone for water or any other
unwanted material in the grease.
(a) If water or unwanted material is found in the grease, remove and replace the entire wheel
assembly.
NOTE: It is normal for the grease color to change from red or light brown to dark brown,
gray, or black. Grease color is not a cause to reject unless the grease color is
white. White color is an indication that grease contains unwanted water.
SUBTASK 32-45-00-210-012
(4) Examine the internal and external surfaces of the bearing cup and cone for any obvious signs
of cracking, flat spots or damage.
(a) If cracking, flat spots or damage is found, remove and replace the entire wheel assembly,
including the wheel bearing cone.
SUBTASK 32-45-00-100-001
(5) Wipe off the grease only from the cup race with a lint-free cloth, G00834.
(a) Remove only enough grease to get a clear view of bearing cup race surface.
(b) Do not use solvents to clean the bearing cup race surface.
SUBTASK 32-45-00-210-013
(6) Visually examine the cup race with a flashlight for marks, discoloration or corrosion. See
(Figure 604) for examples of marks and discolorations.
(a) If no defects are found, do the steps:
1) Re-apply a thin layer of bearing grease Aeroshell 22 grease, D00378, Mobil 28
grease, D00233 or Mobil Aviation Grease SHC 100 grease, D50005 to the surface
of the cup race.
2) Re-insert the wheel bearing cone into the bearing cup.
(b) If discoloration, texture or surface corrosion is found, attempt to remove it by gently using
Scotch-Brite 7447 pad, G51224 or Scotch-Brite 7448 pad, G50492. Perform this task for
no longer than 2 minutes.
1) Equivalent abrasive papers or cloths to the ones given inhere (with a grade between
600 to 1000) can be used instead.
2) Do not use wire metal brushes, rotary brushes or flappers of any kind to perform
this task.
(c) After the area has been reworked, slowly slide a ball point pen, a non-metallic
scraper/pick or a bare fingernail along the whole cup race surface to feel for
abnormalities:
1) If texture is felt, remove and replace the entire wheel assembly including the wheel
bearing cone.
2) If corrosion is still present, remove and replace the entire wheel assembly including
the wheel bearing cone.
3) If no texture is felt, do the steps:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
a) Re-apply a thin layer of bearing grease Aeroshell 22 grease, D00378, Mobil 28
grease, D00233 or Mobil Aviation Grease SHC 100 grease, D50005 to the
surface of the cup race.
b) Re-insert the wheel bearing cone into the bearing cup.

F. Tire Inflation Valve Installation
SUBTASK 32-45-08-210-001
(1) Do a check of the port in the wheel half for cracks, burrs, or scratches propagating from the
port.
(a) If cracks, burrs, or scratches are present, remove the wheel and the tire.
SUBTASK 32-45-08-420-006
(2) If the main and nose wheel assemblies used the tire pressure sensor as an inflation valve [2],
do these steps:
NOTE: There are two configurations available for the tire inflation valve:
• A standard valve
• A combination inflation valve/pressure sensor.
(a) For the Goodrich wheel assembly, do these steps:
1) Apply a thin layer of grease, D00504, for the orange or red packing [1], or PST 525
silicone grease, D50113, for the black packing [1].
2) Prevent contact packing [1] with the thread of the inflation valve [2].
3) Use a socket wrench, STD-7044, to install the inflation valve [2] on the wheel.
4) Tighten the tire inflation valve [2] to 150 in-lb (16.9 N·m) - 200 in-lb (22.6 N·m).
5) Make sure that the red mark on the tire is aligned with the inflation valve [2].
NOTE: The red dot identifies the lightest area of the tire.
6) If it is necessary, install MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, between the inflation
valve [2] and the outboard wheel.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) For the Safran wheel assembly, do these steps:
1) Apply a thin layer of vaseline, D50395, for the red packing [1], or PST 525 silicone
grease, D50113, for the black packing [1].
2) Apply Loctite 242 adhesive, A50584, or Loctite 243 adhesive, A50585, to the
inflation valve [2] threads.
NOTE: It is necessary to install and tighten the inflation valve within 1 minute of the
application of retaining compound. If it is tightened after 1 minute of the
application of retaining compound, the bond of the retaining compound will
not be satisfactory and inflation valve must be removed and installed again.
3) Do not let the primer or retaining compound touch the packing [1].
4) Use a socket wrench, STD-7044, to install the inflation valve [2] on the wheel.
5) Tighten the tire inflation valve [2] to 150 in-lb (16.9 N·m) - 200 in-lb (22.6 N·m).
a) Make sure that the inflation valve [2] was tightened within 1 minute after
application of compound.
6) Make sure that the red mark on the tire is aligned with the inflation valve [2].
NOTE: The red dot identifies the lightest area of the tire.
SUBTASK 32-45-08-420-003
(3) If the inflation valve [2] is not a combination valve and tire pressure sensor, do these steps to
install the inflation valve [2]:
(a) Install the inflation valve [2] to the main wheel assembly.
1) For the Goodrich main wheel assembly, do these steps:
a) Apply a thin layer of grease, D00504, for the orange or red packing [1] or PST
525 silicone grease, D50113, for the black packing [1].
b) Prevent contact packing [1] with the thread of the inflation valve [2].
c) Tighten the tire inflation valve [2].
<1> For wheel assemblies with steel brakes, tighten the inflation valve [2] to
165 in-lb (18.6 N·m)-200 in-lb (22.6 N·m).
<2> For wheel assemblies with carbon brakes, tighten the inflation valve [2]
to 210 in-lb (23.7 N·m).
d) Install MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, between the inflation valve [2] and the
outer wheel.
2) For the Safran main wheel assembly, do these steps:
a) Apply a thin layer of vaseline, D50395, for the red packing [1], or PST 525
silicone grease, D50113, for the black packing [1].
b) Apply Loctite 242 adhesive, A50584, or Loctite 243 adhesive, A50585, to the
tire inflation valve [2] thread.
c) Prevent contact packing [1] with the thread of the inflation valve [2].
d) Tighten the tire inflation valve [2] to 182.7 in-lb (20.6 N·m) - 197.9 in-lb
(22.4 N·m).
3) For the Honeywell main wheel assembly, do these steps:
a) Install the packing [1] on the inflation valve [2].
b) Tighten the tire inflation valve [2] to 150 in-lb (16.9 N·m) - 200 in-lb (22.6 N·m).
c) If it is necessary, install MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(b) Install the inflation valve [2] to the nose wheel assembly.
1) For the Goodrich nose wheel assembly, do these steps:
a) Apply a thin layer of grease, D00504, for the orange or red packing [1], or PST
525 silicone grease, D50113, for the black packing [1].
b) Prevent contact packing [1] with the thread of the inflation valve [2].
c) Tighten the tire inflation valve [2] to 175 in-lb (19.8 N·m).
2) For the Safran nose wheel assembly, do these steps:
a) Apply a thin layer of vaseline, D50395, for the red packing [1], or PST 525
silicone grease, D50113, for the black packing [1].
b) Prevent contact packing [1] with the thread of the inflation valve [2].
c) Tighten the tire inflation valve [2] to 143.4 in-lb (16.2 N·m) - 175.2 in-lb
(19.8 N·m).
3) For the Honeywell nose wheel assembly, do these steps:
a) Install the packing [1] on the inflation valve [2].
b) Tighten the tire inflation valve [2] to 150 in-lb (17 N·m) - 200 in-lb (23 N·m).
c) If it is necessary, install MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048.
SUBTASK 32-45-08-580-002
(4) Inflate the tire (TASK 12-15-51-610-802).
G. Tire Inflation Valve Installation Test
SUBTASK 32-45-08-210-002
(1) Using a bubble soap solution, check for leaks around the base of the tire inflation valve [2].
H. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 32-45-08-580-003
(1) Lower aircraft (TASK 07-11-03-580-801, TASK 07-11-03-580-802).

D. Prepare for the Removal
SUBTASK 32-45-11-480-003
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED IN ALL OF THE
LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR
CAN RETRACT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(1) Make sure that the downlock pins are installed in the nose and main landing gear
(PAGEBLOCK 32-00-01/201).
SUBTASK 32-45-11-480-002
(2) Make sure that the tires have chocks installed around them (PAGEBLOCK 10-11-05/201).
SUBTASK 32-45-11-860-001
(3) Make sure that the parking brake is released.
SUBTASK 32-45-11-580-001
(4) Lift the wheel and tire assemblies with jacks until they are clear of the ground, do this task: Lift
the Main Landing Gear Axles with the Axle Jacks, TASK 07-11-03-580-801.
SUBTASK 32-45-11-860-002
(5) Make sure that the parking brake is set.
NOTE: When you set the parking brake, the brake rotors will be aligned for wheel installation.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 32-45-11-840-001
WARNING
DEFLATE THE TIRE BEFORE YOU REMOVE THE WHEEL AND TIRE
ASSEMBLY. OR, DO AN INSPECTION OF THE WHEEL AND TIRE TO MAKE
SURE THAT THEY ARE SAFE. AIR PRESSURE CAN CAUSE AN EXPLOSION
OF THE DAMAGED WHEEL AND TIRE COMPONENTS. INJURIES TO
PERSONNEL, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
WARNING
REMOVE ONLY ONE WHEEL AND TIRE ASSEMBLY FROM THE MAIN
LANDING GEAR AT A TIME. IF YOU REMOVE THE TWO WHEEL AND TIRE
ASSEMBLIES AT THE SAME TIME, STRUCTURAL DAMAGE AND INJURY TO
PERSONS CAN OCCUR IF THE AIRPLANE FALLS.
(6) Do the following steps to examine the tire and wheel assembly to see if it is safe to remove
without tire deflation, or deflate the tire:
NOTE: If you will not install the same wheel and tire assembly, deflate the tire to prevent
transporting an inflated tire.
(a) Inspect the outboard wheel and tire assembly [1] and/or the inboard wheel and tire
assembly [17] to see if it has the conditions that follow:
1) Inspect the tires and make sure that there are no air leaks, abrasions, unusual worn
areas, cuts or flat spots, do this task: Tires - Inspection, TASK 32-45-00-700-803.
2) Inspect the wheels and make sure that there is no evidence of wheel damage,
including corrosion, loose or damaged or missing tire bolts or tire nuts, overheat
damage or cracks, do this task: Wheels Fast Check (Wheel Installed on the
Airplane), TASK 32-45-00-700-801.
3) If the wheel and tire assembly has any of the conditions in the above steps, you
must deflate the tire.
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT ALL PERSONNEL ARE CLEAR OF THE INFLATION
VALVE ASSEMBLY PATH WHILE YOU REMOVE IT. IF THE INFLATION
VALVE ASSEMBLY EJECTS WHILE YOU REMOVE IT, INJURY TO
PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE DEFLATED TIRE THAT IS ON THE AXLE DOES
NOT TOUCH THE GROUND. IF THE TIRE DOES TOUCH THE GROUND,
THE TIRE'S BEAD SEAT CAN MOVE OUT OF ITS POSITION AND
BECOME UNSEATED. THE UNSEATED BEAD SEAT CAN CAUSE
LEAKAGE WHICH THEN CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE TIRE AND
WHEEL.
CAUTION
DO NOT USE TOO MUCH FORCE ON THE VALVE CORE. THE CORE
PARTS CAN MOVE AND THE SLEEVE AND THE LOWER END OF THE
POPPET WILL STAY IN THE VALVE STEM. IF PARTS STAY IN THE
VALVE STEM, DAMAGE CAN OCCUR TO THE VALVE STEM.
(b) Deflate the tire with the small bore tire deflator, COM-4046, or large bore tire deflator,
COM-1524.
NOTE: If the wheel and tire are not damaged, it is acceptable to leave approximately
50 psi (345 kPa) or 25% of the service pressure in the tire while deflating.
Leaving approximately 50 psi (345 kPa) or 25% of the service pressure in the tire
can prevent damage to the tire when the wheel and tire are transported.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
1) Use the 0-300 psig (0-2069 kpa) tire pressure gauge, STD-1132, to measure the tire
pressure (TASK 12-15-51-780-801).
(c) If you cannot use the usual procedure to deflate the tire because the valve core is
damaged, do these steps:
1) Turn the valve assembly slowly in a counterclockwise direction until there is gas
leakage through the boss.
2) At the same time, push lightly on the valve assembly.
3) After all of the gas has been released, remove the valve assembly from the tire.
E. Main Landing Gear Wheel and Tire Assembly Removal
SUBTASK 32-45-11-020-001
(1) Remove the hubcap [3] from the outboard wheel and tire assembly [1] or hubcap [18] from the
inboard wheel and tire assembly [17], do these steps for the applicable wheel:
(a) For the outboard wheel and tire assembly [1], turn the cam-locs [4] 1/4 turn to disconnect
the hubcap fairing [5] from the hubcap [3].
(b) Remove the lockwire from the bolts [6] (TASK 20-10-44-000-801).
(c) Remove the bolts [6] and washers [7] to disconnect the hubcap from the wheel.
(d) Remove the hubcap from the wheel.
SUBTASK 32-45-11-020-002
(2) Remove the outboard wheel and tire assembly [1] or inboard wheel and tire assembly [17], do
these steps for the applicable wheel:
(a) Remove the nuts [8], washers [9], and bolts [10] that hold the axle nut [16] to the axle.
WARNING
DO NOT PUT FINGERS IN THE LIGHTENING HOLES OF THE WHEEL
RETAINING NUT SOCKET TOOL WHEN YOU REMOVE OR INSTALL THE
WHEEL RETAINING NUT. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS.
(b) Remove the nut [16] with the socket, SPL-1865.
(c) Remove the retention washer [15].
(d) Install the thread protector assembly, of the thread protector, SPL-1876, or the thread
protector, SPL-14320, (for undersized threads) on the axle threads.

G. Prepare for the Installation
SUBTASK 32-45-11-840-003
(1) Do these steps to prepare for installation:
(a) Remove the axle protector assembly, of the thread protector, SPL-1876, from the axle.
(b) Remove all the old grease from the axle.
(c) Remove all the old grease from the inner diameter of the brake.
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT CORRECT PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT IS
USED FOR EYES DURING INSTALLATION AND REMOVAL OF THE
BRAKE ASSEMBLY. IF CORRECT PERSONAL PROTECTIVE
EQUIPMENT IS NOT USED BRAKE DUST CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO
PERSON.
(d) Do an inspection of the brake.
NOTE: Do this inspection with special attention to the whole circumference of each rotor
for the signs of a broken rotor drive clip(s).
1) Do this task: Main Landing Gear Brake Check (Wheel Removed from the Airplane),
TASK 32-41-41-700-803.
(e) Do an inspection of the axle.
(f) Examine the antiskid transducer drive components in the axle and hubcap [3], and
hubcap [18] for damage.




EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(g) If the wheel is not new, inspect the bearings, seals, and other parts of the wheel
assembly.
(h) If the tire is not new, do a tire inspection.
1) Do this task: Tires - Inspection, TASK 32-45-00-700-803.
(i) If it is necessary to install the wheel inboard and outboard bearing assemblies, do these
steps:
1) Apply Aeroshell 22 grease, D00378, or Mobil 28 grease, D00233, or Mobil Aviation
Grease SHC 100 grease, D50005, to all of the parts of the bearing assemblies.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THE CORRECT BEARING IS INSTALLED IN THE
OUTSIDE OF THE WHEEL. INSTALLATION OF THE INNER
BEARING IN THE OUTER BEARING WHEEL LOCATION CAN
CAUSE WHEEL DAMAGE.
2) Install the inner bearing [12] in the inner side of the wheel and the outer bearing [13]
in the outer side of the wheel.
CAUTION
INSTALL THE CORRECT GREASE SEAL IN THE EXTERNAL PART
OF THE WHEEL. INSTALLATION OF THE INNER GREASE SEAL IN
THE OUTER GREASE SEAL WHEEL LOCATION CAN CAUSE SEAL
DAMAGE.
3) Install the grease seal [11] in the inner side of the wheel and the grease seal [14] in
the outer side of the wheel.
4) If part of the assembly, install the retaining ring [19] in the inner side of the wheel
and the retaining ring [20] in the outer side of the wheel.
NOTE: Some wheel assemblies may not have the retaining rings as part of the
configuration, or they may look different from those illustrated.
(j) If using the torque multiplier, inspect the tools before use:
NOTE: This method must only be used if only one engineer is available.
1) Obtain the torque multiplier rig, SPL-15334 (P/N WHEELCHANGEKIT), socket,
SPL-1865, and 110 ft-lbf pre-set torque wrench, SPL-15335 (PART OF
WHEELCHANGEKIT).
2) Check the tooling is serviceable.
3) Check there are no damaged parts.
4) Make sure that the jack extends and retracts.
5) Make sure that the torque multiplier is secure, free to turn and has no damage.
6) If you suspect the torque multiplier is unserviceable (U/S), do not use and return to
stores with a U/S label.
H. Main Landing Gear Wheel and Tire Assembly Installation
SUBTASK 32-45-11-420-001
(1) Do these steps to install the outboard wheel and tire assembly [1] or inboard wheel and tire
assembly [17]:











EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
CAUTION
DO NOT APPLY GREASE TO THE AREA BETWEEN THE AXLE
BEARINGS. HIGH TEMPERATURES IN THIS AREA DURING A LANDING
CAN CAUSE ALL GREASE IN THIS AREA TO BURN. THIS CAN CAUSE
DAMAGE TO WHEELS, TIRES, AND BRAKES.
(a) Apply a thin layer of Aeroshell 22 grease, D00378, or Mobil 28 grease, D00233, or Mobil
Aviation Grease SHC 100 grease, D50005, to the inner diameter surface of the two
bearings where they will touch the axle.
(b) Apply a thin layer of Aeroshell 22 grease, D00378, Mobil 28 grease, D00233, or Mobil
Aviation Grease SHC 100 grease, D50005, to the faces of the washer [15] and nut [16],
and to the axle threads.
(c) Apply a thin layer of Aeroshell 22 grease, D00378, Mobil 28 grease, D00233, or Mobil
Aviation Grease SHC 100 grease, D50005, on the axle where the axle will touch the
wheel bearings.
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT CORRECT PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT IS
USED FOR EYES DURING INSTALLATION AND REMOVAL OF THE
BRAKE ASSEMBLY. IF CORRECT PERSONAL PROTECTIVE
EQUIPMENT IS NOT USED BRAKE DUST CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO
PERSON.
(d) If you need to align the brake disks, do these steps:
1) Release the parking brake.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THE BRAKE ROTORS ARE ALIGNED. DAMAGE TO
THE ROTORS CAN OCCUR IF THE DRIVE KEYS ON THE WHEEL
HIT ROTORS DURING INSTALLATION.
2) Align the brake disks.
3) Set the parking brake.
NOTE: This will keep the brake rotors aligned.
(e) Make sure that the thread protector assembly, of the thread protector, SPL-1876, or
thread protector, SPL-14320, (for undersized threads) is installed.
(f) Install the outboard wheel and tire assembly [1] with the wheel/brake changer dolly,
COM-1818.
1) Make sure that the rotor drive keys on the wheel fully engage the key slots in the
brake rotors.
(g) Remove the thread protector assembly, of the thread protector, SPL-1876, or thread
protector, SPL-14320, (for undersized threads) from the axle threads.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE YOU FIRMLY PUSH BOTH THE WHEEL AND LOCK
WASHER ALL THE WAY ONTO THE AXLE UNTIL THE WHEEL IS SEATED
PRIOR TO INSTALLING AND TIGHTENING THE AXLE NUT. MAKE SURE
THAT THE LOCKTANG IS FIRMLY ENGAGED IN THE KEYWAY GROOVE
IN THE AXLE. DO NOT USE THE AXLE NUT TO PUSH THE WHEEL AND
LOCK WASHER INTO POSITION. FAILURE TO FOLLOW THIS CAN
CAUSE THE WHEEL TO BE LOOSE AND CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE
EQUIPMENT.
(h) Install the washer [15].
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(i) Install the nut [16].
(j) Release the parking brake.
(k) Do these steps to tighten the nut [16] with the torque multiplier (Figure 401 or Figure 402
or Figure 403 or Figure 404):
NOTE: This method must only be used if only one engineer is available.
1) Obtain the torque multiplier rig, SPL-15334 (P/N WHEELCHANGEKIT), socket,
SPL-1865, and 110 ft-lbf pre-set torque wrench, SPL-15335 (PART OF
WHEELCHANGEKIT).
a) Check the condition of the 110 ft-lbf pre-set torque wrench, SPL-15335 (PART
OF WHEELCHANGEKIT), before use.
2) Set up the torque multiplier rig, SPL-15334 (P/N WHEELCHANGEKIT), and make
sure that the ground is level.
3) Align the socket, SPL-1865, with the nut [16].
a) Make sure that the socket, SPL-1865, and the nut [16] are fully engaged.
4) Hold the torque multiplier rig, SPL-15334 (P/N WHEELCHANGEKIT), down
securely by applying foot pressure to the frame where “FOOT STEP” is marked.
NOTE: Foot pressure is applied to prevent possible nut socket disengagement.
CAUTION
WHEN YOU USE A 110 FT-LBS (149 N-M) PRESET TORQUE
WRENCH, DO NOT EXCEED THE PRESET TORQUE VALUE. IF YOU
USE MORE THAN THAT VALUE, IT CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE
AIRCRAFT.
5) Use the 110 ft-lbf pre-set torque wrench, SPL-15335 (PART OF
WHEELCHANGEKIT), to tighten the nut [16].
NOTE: The 110 ft-lbf pre-set torque wrench, SPL-15335 (PART OF
WHEELCHANGEKIT), used with the torque multiplier will produce an
applied torque of 550 ft-lb (746 N·m) to the nut [16].
WARNING
DO NOT PUT FINGERS IN THE LIGHTENING HOLES OF THE WHEEL
RETAINING NUT SOCKET TOOL WHEN YOU REMOVE OR INSTALL THE
WHEEL RETAINING NUT. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS.
(l) Do these steps to tighten the nut [16] with the socket, SPL-1865, and torque wrench,
STD-1021:
1) While you turn the wheel, tighten the nut [16] to 500 ft-lb (678 N·m) - 600 ft-lb
(813 N·m).
2) Stop the wheel.
3) While you turn the wheel, loosen the nut [16] to almost zero torque.
NOTE: The function is to keep the bearing seated.
a) If the nut [16] is set to zero torque, re-seat the wheel.
4) While you turn the wheel, tighten the nut [16] to 150 ft-lb (203 N·m).
5) If the holes for bolt [10] do not align, continue to tighten the nut [16] to align the
holes.
a) Do not tighten the nut [16] to more than 300 ft-lb (407 N·m).
NOTE: The holes will align every 6 degrees that you turn the nut.
























EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(m) Do these steps to install the two bolts [10] to lock the nut [16] to the outboard wheel and
tire assembly [1]:
1) Install the two bolts [10] with the heads to the inside of the axle.
2) Install the washers [9] and nuts [8].
3) Check the self locking nuts (TASK 20-50-11-910-801).
4) Tighten the nuts [8] to 65 ±2 in-lb (7.3 ±0.2 N·m).
NOTE: This is per Standard Torque Values, TASK 20-50-11-910-801 to have the
lowest maximum value when both nuts and the bolts can be tightened.
SUBTASK 32-45-11-420-002
CAUTION
DO NOT TIGHTEN THE HUBCAP BOLTS TOO MUCH. MAKE SURE THAT THE
HUBCAP IS IN THE CORRECT POSITION BEFORE YOU TIGHTEN THE
BOLTS. TOO MUCH TORQUE WILL CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE BOLTS AND
THE HUBCAP.
(2) Install the hubcap [3] or hubcap [18].
(a) Do these steps to install the hubcap [3]:
1) Turn the antiskid transducer dog [2] inside the outboard wheel and tire assembly [1]
such that the drive on the hubcap [3] and antiskid transducer dog [2] in the wheel
will connect when the hubcap [3] is installed.
2) Put the hubcap [3] in its position on the outboard wheel and tire assembly [1].
3) Make sure that the hubcap [3] flush with the outboard wheel and tire assembly [1].
a) Use a soft mallet to lightly tap the hubcap [3] to make it flush.
4) Install the bolts [6] and washers [7] to connect the hubcap [3] to the outboard wheel
and tire assembly [1].
a) Tighten the bolts [6] to 50 in-lb (5.65 N·m) - 80 in-lb (9.04 N·m).
5) Install the lockwire on the bolts [6] (TASK 20-10-44-400-801).
NOTE: The installation of the lockwire is acceptable on the fasteners that are over
6 in. (15 cm) apart at this location.
6) Put the hubcap fairing [5] on the hubcap [3].
7) Turn the cam-locs [4], 1/4 turn to attach the hubcap fairing [5] to the hubcap [3].
(b) Do these steps to install the hubcap [18]:
1) Turn the antiskid transducer dog [2] inside the inboard wheel and tire assembly [17]
such that the drive on the hubcap [18], and the antiskid transducer dog [2] in the
wheel will connect when the hubcap [18] is installed.
2) Put the hubcap [18] in its position on the inboard wheel and tire assembly [17].
3) Make sure that the hubcap [18] flush with the inboard wheel and tire assembly [17].
a) Use a soft mallet to lightly tap the hubcap [18] to make it flush.
4) Install the bolts [6] and washers [7] to connect the hubcap [18] to the inboard wheel
and tire assembly [17].
a) Tighten the bolts [6] to 50 in-lb (5.65 N·m) - 80 in-lb (9.04 N·m).
5) Install the lockwire on the bolts [6] (TASK 20-10-44-400-801).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 32-45-11-610-002
(3) Make sure that the landing gear tire pressure is within the servicing limits
(TASK 12-15-51-780-801).
I. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 32-45-11-580-002
WARNING
MAKE SURE THE AREA AROUND THE TIRES IS CLEAR OF PERSONS AND
EQUIPMENT. IF THE AREA AROUND THE TIRES IS NOT CLEAR, INJURIES
TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
(1) Lower the axle and remove the jacks (TASK 07-11-03-580-801).

D. Prepare for the Removal
SUBTASK 32-45-21-860-002
(1) Make sure that the parking brake is set.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 32-45-21-480-001
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED ON ALL THE
LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR
CAN RETRACT. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS, AND DAMAGE
TO EQUIPMENT.
(2) Make sure that the landing gear downlock downlock equipment, SPL-1880, and NLG towing
lever pin, SPL-1499, are installed, do this task: Landing Gear Downlock Pins Installation,
TASK 32-00-01-480-801.
SUBTASK 32-45-21-480-002
(3) Make sure that the tires of Main Landing Gear (MLG) have the wheel chock, COM-1505,
installed around them (PAGEBLOCK 10-11-05/201).
SUBTASK 32-45-21-580-001
(4) Make sure to lift the nose landing gear and wheel and tire assembly with jacks until they are
clear of the ground (TASK 07-11-03-580-802).
SUBTASK 32-45-21-840-001
WARNING
DEFLATE THE TIRE BEFORE YOU REMOVE THE WHEEL AND TIRE
ASSEMBLY. OR, DO AN INSPECTION OF THE WHEEL AND TIRE TO MAKE
SURE THAT THEY ARE SAFE. AIR PRESSURE CAN CAUSE AN EXPLOSION
OF THE DAMAGED WHEEL AND TIRE COMPONENTS. INJURIES TO
PERSONNEL, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
WARNING
REMOVE ONE WHEEL AND THE TIRE ASSEMBLY FROM THE NOSE
LANDING GEAR AT A TIME. IF YOU REMOVE THE TWO WHEEL AND THE
TIRE ASSEMBLIES AT THE SAME TIME, THE AIRPLANE CAN FALL.
STRUCTURAL DAMAGE AND INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR.
(5) Do the following steps to examine the tire and wheel assembly to see if it is safe to remove
without tire deflation, or deflate the tire (TASK 32-45-00-000-801):
NOTE: If you will not install the same tire and wheel assembly, deflate the tire to prevent
transporting an inflated tire.
(a) Inspect the wheel and tire assembly [1] to see if it has the conditions that follow:
1) Inspect the tires and make sure that there are no air leaks, abrasions, unusual worn
areas, cuts or flat spots, do this task: Tires - Inspection, TASK 32-45-00-700-803.
2) Inspect the wheels and make sure that there is no evidence of wheel damage,
including corrosion, loose or damaged or missing tie bolts or tie nuts, overheat
damage or cracks, do this task: Wheels Fast Check (Wheel Installed on the
Airplane), TASK 32-45-00-700-801.
NOTE: If the wheel and tire assembly has any of the conditions in the above steps,
you must deflate the tire.
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT ALL PERSONNEL ARE CLEAR OF THE INFLATION
VALVE ASSEMBLY PATH WHILE YOU REMOVE IT. IF THE INFLATION
VALVE ASSEMBLY EJECTS WHILE YOU REMOVE IT, INJURY TO
PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(WARNING PRECEDES)
WARNING
BE CAREFUL WHEN DEFLATING TIRES, A FLYING INFLATION VALVE
CAP AND CORE CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT AND INJURY
TO PERSONNEL.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE DEFLATED TIRE THAT IS ON THE AXLE DOES
NOT TOUCH THE GROUND. IF THE TIRE DOES TOUCH THE GROUND,
THE TIRE'S BEAD SEAT CAN MOVE OUT OF ITS POSITION AND
BECOME UNSEATED. THE UNSEATED BEAD SEAT CAN CAUSE
LEAKAGE WHICH THEN CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE TIRE AND
WHEEL.
(b) Deflate the tire with the small bore tire deflator, COM-4046, or large bore tire deflator,
COM-1524.
NOTE: If the wheel and tire are not damaged, it is acceptable to leave approximately
50 psi (345 kPa) or 25% of the service pressure in the tire while deflating.
Leaving approximately 50 psi (345 kPa) or 25% of the service pressure in the tire
can prevent damage to the tire when the wheel and tire is transported.
1) Use the 0-300 psig (0-2069 kpa) tire pressure gauge, STD-1132, to measure the tire
pressure (TASK 12-15-51-780-801).
(c) If you cannot use the usual procedure to deflate the tire because the valve core is
damaged, do these steps:
1) Turn the valve assembly slowly in a counterclockwise direction until there is gas
leakage through the boss.
2) At the same time, push lightly on the valve assembly.
3) After all of the gas has been released, remove the valve assembly from the tire.
E. Nose Landing Gear Wheel and Tire Assembly Removal
SUBTASK 32-45-21-020-001
(1) Do these steps to remove the wheel and tire assembly [1]:
(a) Remove the lockwire from the screws [4].
(b) Remove the screws [4] that hold the axle nut [3] to the axle.
(c) Remove the axle nut [3] with the NLG socket, C32012-3, SPL-1817, from the kit socket,
SPL-1865.
(d) Remove the washer [2].
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE AXLE THREAD PROTECTOR IS INSTALLED
BEFORE YOU REMOVE THE WHEEL/TIRE ASSEMBLY. IF YOU REMOVE
THE TIRE ASSEMBLY WITHOUT THE AXLE THREAD PROTECTOR
INSTALLED, DAMAGE TO THE THREADS OR THE TIRE ASSEMBLY CAN
OCCUR.
(e) Install the thread protector assembly, of the thread protector, SPL-1877, on the axle
threads.
NOTE: You can use tape to hold the thread protector to the axle if it is necessary.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
Table 401/32-45-21-993-801 Nose Landing Gear (NLG) - Thread Protector for Kit C32022-20
Optional Part # (Kit) Actual Tool #
C32022-35 C32022-36
C32022-20 C32022-21
C32022-2 C32022-5
(f) If the axle has undersized threads, install the thread protector, SPL-14582, on the axle
threads.
NOTE: You can use tape to hold the thread protector to the axle.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE TO KEEP CLEARANCE BETWEEN THE NOSE-WHEEL
INNER BEARING AND PAINTED SURFACES OF THE NOSE GEAR AXLE
DURING REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION. FRICTION CAN CAUSE
DAMAGE TO NOSE-WHEEL AXLE PAINT AND OTHER EQUIPMENT.
(g) Use the wheel/brake changer dolly, COM-1818, to lift and remove the wheel and tire
assembly [1].
(h) Remove the wheel and tire assembly [1].
(i) Mark the reason for the tire removal on the tire to aid the inspectors when they examine
the tire.

G. Prepare for the Installation
SUBTASK 32-45-21-000-002
(1) Do these steps to prepare for installation:
(a) Remove the axle thread thread protector, SPL-1877, or thread protector, SPL-14582,
from the axle.
(b) Remove all the old grease from the axle.
(c) If the wheel is not new, inspect the bearings, seals, and other parts of the wheel
assembly.
(d) If the tire is not new, do a tire inspection (TASK 32-45-00-700-803).
(e) Do these steps if the component of the nose wheel assembly (the bearings, the seals,
and other parts) need to be installed:
1) Apply Aeroshell 22 grease, D00378, or Mobil 28 grease, D00233, or Mobil Aviation
Grease SHC 100 grease, D50005, to the inner bearing [8], outer bearing [9], grease
seal [7] and grease seal [10].
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THE CORRECT BEARING IS INSTALLED IN THE
OUTSIDE OF THE WHEEL. INSTALLATION OF THE INNER
BEARING IN THE OUTER BEARING WHEEL LOCATION CAN
CAUSE WHEEL DAMAGE.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
(CAUTION PRECEDES)
CAUTION
MAKE SURE TO KEEP CLEARANCE BETWEEN THE NOSE-WHEEL
INNER BEARING AND PAINTED SURFACES OF THE NOSE GEAR
AXLE DURING REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION. FRICTION CAN
CAUSE DAMAGE TO NOSE-WHEEL AXLE PAINT AND OTHER
EQUIPMENT.
2) Install the inner bearing [8] on the inner side of the wheel and the outer bearing [9]
on the outer side of the wheel.
a) Make sure that the inner bearing is installed on the wheel side opposite
inflation valve.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU INSTALL THE CORRECT GREASE SEAL IN
THE OUTER SIDE OF THE WHEEL. IF YOU INSTALL THE INNER
GREASE SEAL IN THE OUTER GREASE SEAL LOCATION, YOU
CAN CAUSE SEAL DAMAGE.
3) Install the grease seal [7] on the inner side of the wheel and the grease seal [10] on
the outer side of the wheel.
a) Make sure that the tab of grease seal fits indentation of cutout in wheel
housing.
4) Install the retaining ring [11] on the inner side of the wheel and the retaining ring [12]
on the outer side of the wheel.
H. Nose Landing Gear Wheel and Tire Assembly Installation
SUBTASK 32-45-21-420-001
(1) Do these steps to install the wheel and tire assembly [1]:
(a) Inspect the axles for nicks, gouges, and damaged chrome plate.
(b) If the axle spacer is removed, do a general visual inspection of the axles for corrosion
(TASK 32-21-71-200-803).
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE SPACER IS CORRECTLY INSTALLED ON THE
AXLE. THE SPACER CAN MOVE WHEN THE WHEEL AND TIRE
ASSEMBLY IS REMOVED. IF IT IS NOT IN ITS CORRECT POSITION,
THE WHEEL AND TIRE ASSEMBLY WILL NOT INSTALL CORRECTLY.
THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(c) Make sure that the axle spacer [5] is installed on the axle.
NOTE: The axle spacer is inboard of the wheel on the axle. The inner bearing will touch
the spacer when the wheel is installed.
1) For airplanes that use cotter pins, make sure that the three new cotter pins [6] are
installed to hold the spacer on the axle.
NOTE: If you did not remove the axle spacer and it is installed correctly, it is not
necessary to replace the three cotter pins [6].
a) Examine the cotter pins [6] installation to make sure that they do not touch the
torsion link lug during wheel installation.
NOTE: An axle spacer that uses cotter pins has 3 holes.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
2) For airplanes that use lockwire, make sure that MS20995C41 lockwire, G00440, is
installed.
NOTE: If you did not remove the axle spacer and it is installed correctly, it is not
necessary to replace the lockwire.
a) Make sure that to bend the lockwire ends pigtails away from the inboard edge
of the spacer (Figure 401).
b) Examine the completed installation to be sure that the lockwire ends do not
touch the axle, or the torsion link lugs.
c) If necessary, adjust the lockwire to make sure that it does not touch the
landing gear parts during landing gear operations.
NOTE: An axle spacer that uses lockwire has six holes.
WARNING
DO NOT APPLY GREASE TO THE AREA BETWEEN THE AXLE
BEARINGS. HIGH TEMPERATURES IN THIS AREA DURING A LANDING
CAN CAUSE ALL GREASE IN THIS AREA TO BURN. THIS CAN CAUSE
INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
(d) Apply a thin layer of Aeroshell 22 grease, D00378, or Mobil 28 grease, D00233, or Mobil
Aviation Grease SHC 100 grease, D50005, to the face and outer diameter of the
spacer [5].
(e) Apply a thin layer of Aeroshell 22 grease, D00378, or Mobil 28 grease, D00233, or Mobil
Aviation Grease SHC 100 grease, D50005, to the inner diameter surface of the two
bearings where they will touch the axle.
(f) Apply a thin layer of Aeroshell 22 grease, D00378, or Mobil 28 grease, D00233, or Mobil
Aviation Grease SHC 100 grease, D50005, to the faces of the washer [2] and the axle
nut [3], and to the axle threads.
(g) Apply a thin layer of Aeroshell 22 grease, D00378, or Mobil 28 grease, D00233, or Mobil
Aviation Grease SHC 100 grease, D50005, on the axle where the axle will touch the
wheel bearings.
(h) Install the thread protector, thread protector, SPL-1877, or thread protector, SPL-14582 (if
the axle undersized threads).
(i) Use the wheel/brake changer dolly, COM-1818, to install the wheel and tire assembly [1].
(j) Install the wheel and tire assembly [1].
(k) Remove the thread protector assembly, of the thread protector, SPL-1877, from the axle
threads.
(l) Align the key of the washer with the keyway of the axle and install the washer [2].
(m) Install the axle nut [3].
(n) Do these steps to torque the axle nut [3] with the NLG socket, C32012-3, SPL-1817, from
kit socket, SPL-1865:
1) While you turn the wheel, torque the axle nut [3] to 80 ft-lb (108 N·m) - 100 ft-lb
(136 N·m).
a) Stop the wheel.
b) While you turn the wheel, loosen the axle nut [3] to almost zero torque.
c) While you turn the wheel, torque the axle nut [3] to 30 ft-lb (41 N·m).
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
d) Continue to tighten the axle nut [3] until two bolt holes in the nut align with two
threaded holes in the washer [2].
NOTE: Do not torque the nut over 60 ft-lb (81 N·m).
(o) Install the two lock screws [4] to lock the axle nut [3] to the washer [2].
1) Torque the two lock screws [4] to 31.0 in-lb (3.5 N·m) - 38.0 in-lb (4.3 N·m).
(p) Install MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, or MS20995NC32 lockwire, G50347, or
MS20995N32 lockwire, G50177, on the lock screws [4].
(q) Make sure that the tire pressure is a minimum of half the correct pressure
(TASK 12-15-51-780-801).
I. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 32-45-21-580-003
(1) Lower the axle and remove the jacks (TASK 07-11-03-580-802).
SUBTASK 32-45-21-020-002
(2) Remove the NLG towing lever pin, SPL-1499, from the nose wheel steering mechanism
(TASK 32-00-01-080-801).
SUBTASK 32-45-21-000-001
(3) Do this task: Landing Gear Tire Pressure Check and Tire Servicing, TASK 12-15-51-780-801.

(Figure 201)
A. References
Reference Title
32-00-01 P/B 201 LANDING GEAR DOWNLOCK PINS - MAINTENANCE
PRACTICES
B. Location Zones
Zone Area
115 Nose Landing Gear Wheel Well - Left

C. Nose Wheel Spin Brake Lining Removal
SUBTASK 32-45-31-480-002
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT THE DOWNLOCK PINS ARE INSTALLED IN ALL OF THE
LANDING GEAR. WITHOUT THE DOWNLOCK PINS, THE LANDING GEAR
CAN RETRACT AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
EQUIPMENT.
(1) Make sure that the downlock pins are installed in the nose and main landing gear
(PAGEBLOCK 32-00-01/201).
SUBTASK 32-45-31-020-001
(2) Remove the screws [6], washers [1], and nuts [2] that hold the spin brake lining [5] to the spin
brake spring [3].
SUBTASK 32-45-31-020-002
(3) Remove the spin brake lining [5] and spacers [4].
32-45-31-400-801Nose Wheel Spin Brake Lining - InstallationPDF p. 1862

D. Procedure
SUBTASK 32-45-31-420-001
(1) Apply sealant, A00247 to the six locations on the spin brake spring [3] where you will install the
spacers [4].
SUBTASK 32-45-31-420-002
(2) Hold the spin brake lining [5] in its position on the spin brake spring [3].
SUBTASK 32-45-31-420-003
(3) Do these steps for each screw [6]:
(a) Install two spacers [4] between the block and the spin brake spring [3] where you will
install the screw [6].
(b) Install the screw [6] and washer [1] through the spin brake lining [5], spacers [4], and the
spin brake spring [3].
(c) Install the washer [1] and the nut [2] on the screw [6].

B. Procedure
SUBTASK 32-45-31-220-001
(1) Measure the distance from the head of each bolt [6] to the wear surface of the spin brake lining
[5].
SUBTASK 32-45-31-350-001
(2) If this distance you measured is less than 0.060 inches (1.524 mm) you must replace that spin
brake lining [5]:
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL

G. Adjust the Interconnect Mechanism for the Rudder Pedals
SUBTASK 32-51-00-020-001
(1) Remove the turnbuckle locking clips from the turnbuckles on the NGPP-A and NGPP-B cables.
SUBTASK 32-51-00-020-002
(2) Remove the nut [7], washer [6], and bolt [5] to disconnect the idler rod on the rudder pedal
interconnect mechanism from the structure.
SUBTASK 32-51-00-220-001
(3) Make sure the rotary actuator is turned in the counter-clockwise direction with the index marks
aligned to show that it is in the air mode.
SUBTASK 32-51-00-480-021
(4) Install rig pins NS1 and NS5. Do the following steps:
(a) Install the rig pin NS1, rigging pin kit, SPL-1585.
(b) Do this task: Put the Airplane in the Air Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-801.
1) Make sure the interconnect eccentric drum rig pin hole and bracket rig pin slot line
up.
(c) Install rig pin NS5
SUBTASK 32-51-00-820-003
(5) Adjust the tension in cables NGPP-A and NGPP-B until the load necessary to move the cable
0.45 in. (11.4 mm) to 0.55 in. (14.0 mm) downward at the turnbuckle is 16 lbf (71.2 N) to 22 lbf
(97.9 N) (as measured with a spring scale, STD-5505).
NOTE: It is not necessary to allow for the temperature because the NGPP cables are very
short.
SUBTASK 32-51-00-080-001
(6) Remove the rig pin NS5.
EFFECTIVITY
 ALL
SUBTASK 32-51-00-710-001
(7) Operate the rotary actuator five times from the air mode, (do this task: Put the Airplane in the
Air Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-801), back to the ground mode, (do this task: Return the
Airplane to the Ground Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-802), and back again.
(a) Make sure the rotary actuator changes from the air mode to the ground mode, and back
again each time.
SUBTASK 32-51-00-210-001
(8) Make sure that the rig pin NS5 fits freely. Do the following steps:
(a) Do this task: Put the Airplane in the Air Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-801.
(b) Make sure the interconnect eccentric drum rig pin hole and bracket rig pin slot line up.
(c) Make sure rig pin NS5 can be installed and removed freely.
SUBTASK 32-51-00-820-024
(9) Make sure the tension in the cables NGPP-A and NGPP-B is such that the load necessary to
move the cable 0.45 in. (11.4 mm) to 0.55 in. (14.0 mm) at the turnbuckle is 16 lbf (71.2 N) to
22 lbf (97.9 N) (as measured with a spring scale, STD-5505).
(a) If it is necessary, adjust the cable turnbuckles until the rig pin NS5 is free and the tension
in the cables is correct.
SUBTASK 32-51-00-820-002
(10) Adjust the length of the idler rod, if it is necessary, so that the bolt [5] fits freely when it is
installed through the rod end and the structure.
(a) Install the bolt [5], washer [6], and nut [7] to attach the idler rod to the structure.
SUBTASK 32-51-00-080-013
(11) Make sure the rig pin NS1 fits freely.
SUBTASK 32-51-00-080-014
(12) Remove rig pin NS1.
SUBTASK 32-51-00-420-008
(13) Install the turnbuckle locking clips on the turnbuckles for the NGPP-A and NGPP-B cables.
SUBTASK 32-51-00-410-009
(14) Close these access panels:
Number Name/Location
113AC Fwd Nose Wheel Well Upper Access Panel
113AW Forward Nose Wheel Well Panel
113BW Forward Nose Wheel Well Panel
(a) Do this task: Nose Wheel Well Access Panels - Installation, TASK 53-14-01-420-801.
SUBTASK 32-51-00-860-044
(15) Do this task: Return the Airplane to the Ground Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-802.

WARNING

(d) Rig pin NS4 in the summing mechanism bracket at the steering metering valve.

1) Make sure that the pointer on the Captain's control wheel is within the CENTER
